## 是什么

unZipro 是一个基于 PyTorch 的轻量级图神经网络（GNN）框架，用于无监督零样本逆折叠（inverse folding）蛋白质进化与高适应度变异预测。它直接从蛋白质结构出发，无需大量实验数据即可优先排序高适应度突变，适用于酶工程、基因组编辑工具、植物蛋白工程、蛋白治疗、合成生物学、蛋白互作工程和农业生物技术等广泛场景。

## 亮点

- **零样本迁移**：无需大量实验数据或 few-shot 训练即可预测功能变异，显著降低筛选成本（最少约 10 个变体）。
- **高准确率**：平均 61% 的高适应度突变（>1.1× WT）成功预测，部分案例达到 100% 成功和 28 倍性能提升。
- **结构灵活**：支持实验解析结构和 AlphaFold 预测模型。
- **元学习适应**：通过 meta-learning 快速适应家族特异的适应度景观。
- **高效工程化**：提供 Docker 镜像、Colab notebook、一键安装脚本，支持 GPU 加速。

## 为何对本课题有用

unZipro 直接面向蛋白质结构 × AI/计算模拟课题，其核心是逆折叠（从结构预测序列）与高适应度变异优先排序，与蛋白质结构设计、序列设计、蛋白-蛋白互作工程高度相关。它展示了如何将通用逆折叠约束与家族特异适应度景观结合，实现零样本变异预测，为蛋白质工程提供高效的计算筛选方法。其 GNN 架构和元学习策略可迁移到其他结构感知的蛋白质设计任务。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：`script/main.py` 用于推理；`script/unZipro_pretrain.py` 用于预训练；`script/unZipro_finetuning.py` 用于微调。
- **安装**：通过 `bash runs/install_unZipro.sh` 或 `pip install -r requirements.txt`，依赖见 `requirements.txt`（PyTorch 2.4.1+cu124、numpy、pandas、biotite 等）。
- **推理示例**：
  ```bash
  python script/main.py --pdb 6vpcE --pdb_dir data/example/ --outdir data/outputs/ --work_dir data/tmp --pretrained --rank_by_prob --logits --probs
  ```
- **输入/输出**：输入为 PDB 结构文件（目录由 `--pdb_dir` 指定）；输出为 CSV 文件，包含每个残基的突变概率/ logits（`*.info_probs.csv`、`*.info_logits.csv`）和排序后的高适应度突变列表（`*.info_rank_by_prob.csv`）。
- **GPU 需求**：推荐 GPU > 32 GB 内存，支持 CPU 模式（`--cpu_only`）。
- **示例脚本**：`runs/run_ABE.sh`、`runs/run_nuclease.sh`、`runs/run_luciferase.sh` 等，覆盖多种蛋白质工程场景。
- **测试**：`tests/` 目录包含测试文件（如 `test_fetch_pdb.py`、`test_finetuning.py` 等），可用于断点调试。

## 核心 idea

unZipro 的核心方法学在于将逆折叠的通用约束与元学习驱动的家族特异适应度景观相结合，实现零样本高适应度突变优先排序。它通过 GNN 从蛋白质结构提取几何特征，利用预训练捕获通用适应度景观，再通过 meta-learning 快速适应特定家族，从而在无需大量实验数据的情况下高效筛选高适应度变异。

## 可搬移点

- **GNN 逆折叠模型**（`script/model/unZipro.py` 等）：可解耦为独立的序列设计模块，用于结构到序列的生成。
- **元学习适应模块**（`script/learn2learn/` 中的 MAML 实现）：可移植到其他蛋白质设计任务，实现快速适应新家族。
- **特征化工具**（`script/utils/featurizer.py`）：从 PDB 结构构建图特征，可复用于其他结构感知模型。
- **Foldseek 集成**（`script/foldseek_api.py`、`script/parse_foldseek_results.py`）：用于结构相似性搜索，可迁移到同源结构检索。
- **License**：Apache 2.0，允许自由使用和修改，但需确认具体条款。

以上模块均可通过逐步替换的方式集成到自定义 Pipeline 中，实现结构感知的蛋白质工程。
readme: # unZipro [![Open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/Gabriel-QIN/unZipro/blob/master/notebooks/unZipro.ipynb) [![Server Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/Website-unZipro-green)](https://ai4bio.online/unZipro/home) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/-GitHub-181717?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Gabriel-Qin/unZipro) [![Python Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.7%2B-blue)](https://www.python.org/) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0) > Official PyTorch implementation of **unZipro** — an unsupervised zero-shot inverse folding framework for protein evolution and high-fitness variant prediction. --- ![unZipro](image/graph.jpg) ## Table of contents - [Overview](#overview) - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Key features](#key-features) - [Applications](#applications) - [Google Colab](#google-colab) - [Run unZipro locally](#run-unzipro-on-local-machine) - [High-fitness mutation prioritization](#high-fitness-mutation-prioritization) - [Pretraining](#pretraining) - [Finetuning](#finetuning) - [Acknowledgements](#acknowledgements) - [Citation](#citation) # Overview unZipro (unsupervised Zero-shot inverse folding framework for protein evolution) is a lightweight graph neural network (GNN)-based framework designed for AI-guided protein engineering. By combining general inverse folding constraints with family-specific adaptation, unZipro can efficiently prioritizes high-fitness mutations without exhaustive screening. ![unZipro](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/Gabriel-QIN/unZipro@master/image/unZipro.jpg) ## ⚙️ How it works unZipro tackles protein engineering like “hunting for the needle in the haystack”: - 🧠 Zero-shot transfer learning captures a universal protein fitness landscape. - 🧩 Meta-learning adapts to family-specific fitness landscapes. - Prioritization of the most promising high-fitness variants for experimental validation. ## 🚀 Key Features of unZipro 1. Zero-shot transfer – predict functional variants without extensive few-shot training or large experimental datasets. 2. Highly efficient – drastically reduces experimental screening (as few as ~10 variants) and computational costs. 3. High accuracy – achieves an average of 61% success for high-fitness mutations (>1.1× WT), with up to 100% success and 28× improvement in desired properties. 4. Broad applicability – experimentally validated across enzyme, nucleases, polymerases, transcription factors, virus-resistance proteins, with potential for more protein engineering applications. 5. Structure-flexible: supports both experimentally-resoveled structures and AlphaFold-predicted models. ## Applications unZipro is a general-purpose framework for in silico protein evolution and can be applied to a broad range of protein engineering tasks, including: - **Enzyme engineering** – activity, stability, specificity, and rate-limiting enzymes. - **Genome editing tools** – CRISPR-Cas systems, base editors, and prime editors. - **Plant protein engineering** – disease resistance, transcription factors, and metabolic enzymes. - **Protein therapeutics** – antibodies, therapeutic enzymes, cytokines, and peptides. - **Synthetic biology** – metabolic pathways, biosensors, and regulatory proteins. - **Protein interaction engineering** – protein–ligand and protein–nucleic acid interactions. - **Agricultural biotechnology** – crop improvement and stress tolerance. - **General protein design** – beneficial mutation discovery for diverse proteins. ![applications](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/Gabriel-QIN/unZipro@master/image/applications.jpg) # Google Colab [![Open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/Gabriel-QIN/unZipro/blob/master/notebooks/unZipro.ipynb) We provide a convenient [Google Colab notebook](https://colab.research.google.com/github/Gabriel-QIN/unZipro/blob/master/notebooks/unZipro.ipynb) to run unZipro on-the-fly without any local installation. > For optimal performance when running unZipro, we strongly recommend using a GPU with > 32 GB of memory. This ensures sufficient memory to handle complex computations and avoid memory errors. # Run unZipro on local machine ## Installation ### Anaconda Please first install [Anaconda](https://www.anaconda.com/download) or [Miniconda](https://docs.conda.io/en/latest/miniconda.html). Then create and activate a conda enviroment as follows: ```sh git clone https://github.com/Gabriel-Qin/unZipro.git cd unZipro # Install dependencies and PyTorch automatically bash runs/install_unZipro.sh ``` Alternatively, you can manually install all dependencies with: ```sh pip install -r requirements.txt ``` unZipro requires Python >= 3.9 and is compatible with PyTorch versions later than 2.0. Users should install the appropriate [PyTorch](https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/) and [CUDA](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-downloads) versions according to your local hardware and driver environment. Example installation for PyTorch with CUDA 12.4: ```sh pip install torch==2.4.1+cu124 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124 ``` After installation, verify the environment with: ```sh python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available())" # Expected output: `2.4.1+cu124 True` ``` This confirms that PyTorch is correctly installed and GPU acceleration is available. ### Docker A Docker image is provided to ensure a reproducible runtime environment without manually configuring dependencies. Please configure your Docker environment according to the official documentation for [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) and [NVIDIA Container Toolkit](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/container-toolkit/latest/install-guide.html) #### Pull image ```sh docker pull crpi-d49mzvu99jzxukne.cn-hongkong.personal.cr.aliyuncs.com/gabrielqin/unzipro:latest docker tag crpi-d49mzvu99jzxukne.cn-hongkong.personal.cr.aliyuncs.com/gabrielqin/unzipro:latest unzipro:latest ``` #### Test GPU availability ```sh docker run --rm --gpus all \ unzipro:latest \ python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())" # Expected output is True ``` #### Start container ```sh docker run --rm --gpus all -it \ -v $(pwd):/workspace/unZipro \ -w /workspace/unZipro \ unzipro:latest \ bash ``` ## High-fitness mutation prioritization > unZipro predicts and prioritizes beneficial mutations directly from protein structures, enabling structure-aware protein engineering without supervised fine-tuning. ### Inference: #### Local environment ```sh python script/main.py --pdb 6vpcE --pdb_dir data/example/ --outdir data/outputs/ --work_dir data/tmp --pretrained --rank_by_prob --logits --probs ``` #### Docker ```sh docker tag crpi-d49mzvu99jzxukne.cn-hongkong.personal.cr.aliyuncs.com/gabrielqin/unzipro:latest unzipro:latest docker run --rm --gpus all -it unzipro:latest \ python script/main.py \ --pdb 6vpcE \ --pdb_dir data/example/ \ --outdir data/outputs/ \ --work_dir data/tmp \ --pretrained \ --rank_by_prob \ --logits \ --probs ``` Input flags: - `--pdb` PDB name(s) for inference. Supports comma-separated PDB IDs or a text file containing multiple IDs. - `--pdb_dir` Directory containing input PDB structure files. - `--outdir` Directory for saving prediction outputs. - `--work_dir` Temporary working directory for intermediate files. - `--pretrained` Use the pretrained inverse folding model directly for mutation prioritization without fine-tuning. - `--rank_by_prob` Rank candidate mutations according to predicted mutation probabilities. Additional optional flags: - `--gpu` / `--cpu_only` Specify GPU device ID or force CPU-only inference. - `--probs` / `--logits` Output per-residue mutation probabilities or raw logits. - `--res` Restrict prediction outputs to specific residues (e.g., `83,123`). - `--epochs`, `--adapt_lr`, `--meta_lr`, `--adapt_step` Hyperparameters for meta-transfer fine-tuning. - `--batchsize`, `--patience`, `--noise` Training batch size, early stopping patience, and training noise level. - `--nneighbor` Number of neighboring residues used in graph construction. - `--skip_foldseek` Skip Foldseek search if precomputed results are already available. - `--save_model_ckp` Save model checkpoints during training. The outputs include: - Per-residue mutation probabilities/logits at `data/outputs/{your_protein_name}.info_probs.csv` and `data/outputs/{your_protein_name}.info_logits.csv!` - Ranked potential high-fitness mutations at `data/outputs/{your_protein_name}.info_rank_by_prob.csv` Following are some provided `examples`: | Category | Script | Description | | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | | **Genome editors** | [`runs/run_ABE.sh`](runs/run_ABE.sh) | Adenine base editor (TadA8e) | | | [`runs/run_nuclease.sh`](runs/run_nuclease.sh) | Three nucleases (SpCas9, CasΦ2/Cas12j2, T5E) | | | [`runs/run_polymerase.sh`](runs/run_polymerase.sh) | MMLV reverse transcriptase under multiple conformations | | **Fluorescent enzyme** | [`runs/run_luciferase.sh`](runs/run_luciferase.sh) | Luciferase for improved fluorescence intensity | | **Plant proteins** | [`runs/run_plantTF.sh`](runs/run_plantTF.sh) | DNA-binding domains of plant transcription factors | | | [`runs/run_R_protein.sh`](runs/run_R_protein.sh) | Plant virus-resistance (R) proteins | ## Pretraining You can reproce the unZipro pre-training and evaluation following the instructions from [Pre-training](docs/pretrain.md). ### Pretrain on PDB50 datasets #### 1. Download full PDB50 dataset ```python python script/fetch_PDB_parallel.py -i data/pretrained/all_PDB50.txt -o data/pretrained/PDB -m RCSB -cpu 8 ``` #### 2. Start pre-training ```python python script/unZipro_pretrain.py \ --train_list data/pretrained/train.txt \ --valid_list data/pretrained/valid.txt \ --pdbdir data/pretrained/PDB \ --epochs 100 \ --batchsize 10 \ --model Models \ --cachedir data/pretrained/tmp/ \ --project_name unZipro_pretrain ``` #### 3. Evaluate the pre-trained model You can evaluate the pre-trained unZipro model on a single benchmark dataset, for example TS50, by running: ``` dataset=TS50 python script/unZipro_evaluate.py --project_name unZipro_${dataset}_test \ --input data/pretrained/benchmark/${dataset}.txt \ --pdbdir data/pretrained/benchmark/${dataset} \ --outdir outputs/seq_design \ --config_path config/unZipro_pretrain.json \ --param Models/unZipro_params.pt \ --gpu 0 \ --sampling_strategy argmax ``` #### 4. Batch evaluation on multiple benchmarks To conveniently evaluate the model across multiple benchmark datasets (e.g., PDB50), you can run the provided shell script: ```sh bash runs/evaluate_pretrained_model.sh ``` Or pre-train on your own structure dataset ```python python script/unZipro_pretrain.py \ --train_list data/pretrained/train.txt \ --valid_list data/pretrained/valid.txt \ --pdbdir data/pretrained/PDB \ --epochs 100 \ --batchsize 10 \ --model Models \ --cachedir data/pretrained/tmp/ \ --project_name unZipro_pretrain ``` ## Finetuning Run unZipro fine-tuning easily with the following command. ``` # Before runnning, you must prepare your train/valid dataset (each file with corresponding PDB IDs) # Or you can use the Foldseek-retrieved structures as your fine-tuninng datasets. # Please ensure your PDB files are in `pdbdir` name=ABE python script/unZipro_finetuning.py --train data/finetuned_dataset/${name}/train.csv --valid data/finetuned_dataset/${name}/test.csv --pdbdir data/finetuned_dataset/PDB --cache_dir data/finetuned_dataset/tmp --model Models/finetuned/ABE --project_name unZipro_ABE --epochs 20 --gpu 0 --first_order --batchsize 1 ``` Or you can simply run this bash script (every step will be excuted here): ```bash bash runs/finetune_ABE.sh ``` For more details, see [Finetuning](docs/finetuning.md). ## Acknowledgements We gratefully acknowledge the open-source community for providing valuable tools and insights that inspired the development of unZipro. This work builds upon ideas and methodologies introduced by previous research in AI/ML, protein design, and AIxbio community. In particular, we recognize the contributions of prior works including many graph-based protein design frameworks and Foldseek, which have laid the foundation for advances in structure-informed protein engineering. We sincerely thank the authors of these repositories for their pioneering efforts and their invaluable contributions to the broader scientific community. ## Citation If you use **unZipro** in your research, please cite: > Qin, Z., Zhao, S., Deng, Z., Si, X., Cheng, X., Zhang, Z., Zhang, Y., Han, X., Zhang, J., Chen, Y., Liu, X., Li, J., Fu, L., You, L., Murray, J. W., Liu, H., Li, H., Li, C., Wu, S., Li, J., Chen, Z., Song, J., Wang, D., & Ji, X. > Simplifying in silico protein evolution with minimal screening by unZipro. *Molecular Cell*,**86** (20), 4183–4199.e12. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.molcel.2026.08.028 ## License Distributed under [Apache 2.0](https://github.com/Gabriel-QIN/unZipro/blob/master/LICENSE) license.

## 是什么

RainMD 是一个基于 WebGPU 的浏览器端分子动力学（MD）模拟引擎，直接从 AMBER 拓扑文件（`.prmtop`）和坐标文件（`.crd`）出发，在用户自己的 GPU 上运行完整的 MD 模拟流程（最小化、平衡、生产），无需安装任何软件或排队等待。它旨在将 MD 模拟的门槛降低到“打开网页、拖入文件”即可运行，同时保证数据隐私（默认不离开本地机器）。

## 亮点

- **纯浏览器 GPU 计算**：利用 WebGPU 在浏览器中直接调用 GPU，实现力场计算和积分器全在设备端执行，无服务器依赖，无网络请求（默认）。
- **高精度复现**：能量和力与 OpenMM 的差异分别达到 1.4e-6 和 8.8e-5，DCD 轨迹文件与 OpenMM 输出字节级一致。
- **高性能**：在 Apple 笔记本 GPU 上，1190 原子测试系统达到约 133 ns/day，比宿主参考快约 60 倍。
- **实时分析面板**：模拟过程中实时绘制 RMSD、回旋半径、势能、残基 RMSF、界面距离和温度等六个面板，并支持多种 RMSD 拆分方式（整体、受体、结合体、受体拟合结合体）。
- **完整工作流**：内置最小化、NPT 平衡（带约束）、NPT 生产三个阶段，并支持暂停/恢复，输出 DCD、AMBER 重启文件、PDB 和 CSV 指标。
- **零构建、零安装**：静态文件即可运行，无构建步骤，适合教学和快速验证。

## 为何对本课题有用

RainMD 直接服务于蛋白质结构 × AI/计算模拟课题中的 MD 模拟环节。它提供了一个可移植的 GPU 加速 MD 引擎，能够：

- **加速构象采样**：在浏览器中快速运行 MD，用于生成蛋白质构象集合，为结构预测或生成模型提供训练数据或验证集。
- **验证 AI 预测结构**：对 AlphaFold 等预测的蛋白质结构进行 MD 弛豫和稳定性评估，检查其物理合理性。
- **研究蛋白-蛋白相互作用**：通过实时界面距离面板，直接观察结合体在模拟中的稳定性，辅助对接结果验证。
- **降低计算门槛**：无需高性能计算集群，即可在个人设备上运行小规模 MD，适合教学和快速原型验证。
- **可迁移的 GPU 计算模式**：其“GPU-resident”设计（力与积分全在设备端）和 WebGPU 实现，可借鉴到其他 AI/计算模拟工具中，实现浏览器端推理或采样。

## 怎么用

- **运行**：克隆仓库后，执行 `python3 tools/serve.py`，然后浏览器打开 `http://127.0.0.1:4173/`。需要支持 WebGPU 的浏览器（Chrome/Edge 113+，Safari 18+）。
- **输入**：AMBER 拓扑文件（`.prmtop`）和坐标文件（`.crd`），可通过拖拽上传。仓库自带测试系统（如溶剂化丙氨酸二肽），可直接加载。
- **输出**：DCD 轨迹文件、AMBER 重启文件、PDB 文件（当前视图）、CSV 指标文件（RMSD、RMSF 等）。
- **测试**：
  - `npm run test:ci`：约 12 秒，无需 GPU，覆盖宿主套件、OpenMM 对比、解析器测试。
  - `npm run test:gpu`：15 个内核检查，需要 WebGPU 设备。
  - `npm run test:slow`：约 9 分钟，需要 GPU，覆盖 NPT 盒、温度、能量漂移等。
- **调试**：可运行 `npm run check:openmm` 对比 OpenMM 能量/力，`npm run check:gradients` 验证解析力与数值梯度。
- **依赖**：Node.js ≥ 20，Python 3（用于服务脚本），无其他构建依赖。

## 核心 idea

RainMD 的核心洞察是：**将 MD 模拟的“重活”前置到离线阶段，浏览器只负责执行**。它借鉴了 LocalFold 的思路——AMBER 拓扑文件（`.prmtop`）被视为“权重包”，包含了力场参数、电荷和原子类型等所有必要信息，而浏览器端只需解析并执行 GPU 计算。这使得复杂的 MD 模拟可以在无服务器、无安装的浏览器环境中运行，同时保持与 OpenMM 等专业工具的高精度一致性。其方法学在于：通过精心设计的 GPU 内核（如 PME、非键相互作用）和高效的块级命令缓冲，实现了在 WebGPU 上的高性能计算，并通过分层测试（宿主 vs GPU）确保正确性。

## 可搬移点

- **AMBER 解析器**（`shared/amber/`）：可独立提取，用于任何需要解析 `.prmtop` 和 `.crd` 的 Pipeline，支持自定义力场加载。
- **GPU 内核**（`webgpu/kernels/`）：包括 PME、非键相互作用、积分器等，可移植到其他 WebGPU 或 GPU 计算框架中，用于加速 MD 或相关计算。
- **实时分析模块**（`shared/analysis/`）：RMSD、RMSF、回旋半径等计算逻辑，可复用于其他模拟或 AI 生成结构的评估。
- **DCD 写入器**（`shared/traj/dcd.js`）：可独立使用，用于生成标准轨迹文件。
- **License**：MIT，允许自由使用和修改，但需注意 AMBER 力场参数有其自身许可条款，仓库未包含除测试系统外的参数。

**可迁移性评估**：RainMD 的模块化设计（`shared`、`cpu`、`webgpu` 分层）使其易于拆解和逐步替换。例如，可以将 `shared/` 中的解析器和分析模块直接 import 到自定义 Python 或 Node.js Pipeline 中，而 GPU 内核可作为参考实现。但需注意，其核心模拟逻辑与 WebGPU 紧密耦合，若需在其他平台使用，可能需要重写设备层。

# RainMD

### → **[Run it: pablo-arantes.github.io/rainmd](https://pablo-arantes.github.io/rainmd/)**

Molecular dynamics that runs **in your browser**, on your own GPU, from the
AMBER topology you already have. No install and no queue.

Nothing leaves your machine unless you ask it to: the page is static files, the
simulation runs on your GPU, the trajectory is written in your browser, and
opening the page makes no network request at all. There is nowhere a structure
is sent by default. The one exception is deliberate and opt-in — a **Share to
LogMD** button that posts frames to a third party, which the page itself
explains before you press it. If you have no AMBER files to hand, the page
offers the systems this repository tests itself against; load one and the
solvated alanine dipeptide runs a real NPT simulation.

Needs a browser with WebGPU: Chrome or Edge 113+, or Safari 18+. On Linux,
Chrome may still need `--enable-unsafe-webgpu`.

The simulation is GPU-resident: forces *and* integration run on the device, and
a block of steps is encoded into one command buffer, so there is no per-step
round trip. In NPT — which is the default — the barostat is the one exception:
a Metropolis test is a decision about a number, so the trial energy comes back
to the browser once per volume move, every 25 steps by default. Measured, that
costs 0.167 ms/step. It reproduces OpenMM's energies to
1.4e-6 and its per-atom forces to 8.8e-5 on the notebooks' own configuration,
and runs the 1190-atom test system at **about 133 ns/day** on an Apple laptop
GPU — roughly 60x the host reference it is checked against. Throughput falls
with system size: the same solute in a 12 Å water box is 2854 atoms and
74 ns/day. A literature-length production is not reachable here for a solvated
protein, and the page tells you what your own system will cost before you
start.

A run on the page writes a **DCD trajectory and an AMBER restart**, so the
output goes straight into cpptraj, MDAnalysis, VMD or PyMOL alongside the
`.prmtop` you already have — the DCD writer is byte-compared against OpenMM's
own.

The whole workflow is on the GPU and follows the notebooks' three stages:
**minimise** (steps you choose, 10 kJ/mol/nm tolerance), **equilibrate** in NPT
with the solute's heavy atoms restrained so the water settles around a held
structure, then **production** in NPT with the restraint off. Durations are in
nanoseconds, trajectory intervals in picoseconds, and the page tells you what
each stage will cost at a rate it measures on your own system — because the
honest answer for a solvated protein is often days, and you should see that
before you start. In NPT at 1 bar it took the test
system's deliberately underdense tleap box from 0.587 g/cm³ to **1.001 ± 0.013
g/cm³** over 300 ps, against OpenMM's 0.9997 ± 0.014 on the same system — and
the volume *fluctuation* implies an isothermal compressibility of 4.8e-5 /bar
against water's experimental 4.5e-5, which is the sharper test of the two.
TIP3P wants about 0.98–1.00.

**And you watch the analysis, not just the structure.** While the run is going
the page draws six live panels — RMSD, radius of gyration, potential energy,
per-residue RMSF, interface distance and temperature — and splits the RMSD
**four ways**: the whole complex, the receptor, the binder, and the binder
*fitted on the receptor*. That last one is the number that says whether a pose is
holding: a whole-complex RMSD averages the binder's drift over every receptor
atom that did not move, so a complex coming apart reads as a small number. The
structure view switches between solute, protein + ligand, ligand, backbone and
heavy atoms, solvent excluded by default, and colours by element, by body, or by
**secondary structure**. The structure is drawn by
[Mol*](https://molstar.org/) — RCSB's own renderer, vendored under MIT so the
page needs no network — with its own secondary-structure assignment. It appears
as loaded, after minimisation and at the end of each stage, or every frame if
you ask it to animate. Because an AMBER topology carries no chain IDs, the
receptor/binder split is derived from the molecule partition and is **yours to
override**: the page offers the molecule list, named by its residues, in place
of the chain letters a PDB-based tool would ask for.
Pause holds the integrator between blocks and resumes from the identical state.
Everything exports: DCD, AMBER restart, a PDB of exactly the atoms on screen,
and the metrics and RMSF as CSV.

That design is [JIGGLE](https://github.com/BioCoder007/JIGGLE)'s, read as
source; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` says which five things were taken from it and the
one it asks for that an AMBER topology cannot answer.

[docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) says exactly what is measured and what is not;
read it before trusting a number.

## The idea

[LocalFold](https://github.com/sokrypton/localfold) runs AlphaFold in a browser
tab on WebGPU. It cannot train a model in the page, so it does not try: the
weights are produced offline and the page runs inference on them.

Molecular dynamics has the same shape. A browser cannot run `tleap`,
`antechamber` or an AM1-BCC charge fit — but it does not need to. The
[Making-it-rain](https://github.com/pablo-arantes/making-it-rain) notebooks
already produce the artifact that matters:

```
Colab notebook (tleap / antechamber / GAFF2)  →  SYS.prmtop + SYS.crd
                                                      │  drag and drop
                                                      ▼
                              browser: parse → GPU buffers → simulate
```

**The prmtop is the weight bundle.** The expensive, irreproducible-in-a-page
work happens once, offline; what crosses into the browser is the result. That
means the same force field, the same charges and the same ligand parameters as
the Colab run — exactly, not approximately — and it means ligands work from day
one.

Why this is worth doing: WebGPU runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, on AMD, Intel,
NVIDIA and Apple silicon, with nothing to install. Anyone with a laptop and a
topology can run a simulation on hardware they already own.

## Running it

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pablo-arantes/rainmd && cd rainmd
python3 tools/serve.py          # then open http://127.0.0.1:4173/
```

Static files, no build step — a plain file server works too, but `serve.py`
sends `no-store` so an edit is not hidden by Chrome's module cache.

Needs a browser with WebGPU: Chrome or Edge 113+, or Safari 18+.

## Checking it yourself

Every claim in [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) is a command, and the commands
are grouped into three lanes by what they need to run.

**`npm run test:ci`** — about 12 seconds, no GPU and no Python. The host suite,
the per-term comparison against OpenMM's committed reference dumps, every
analytic force against a numerical gradient, and the triclinic oracles. This is
the lane `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every push, because nothing in it
imports a package: every specifier is relative or a `node:` builtin, which is
the same no-build-step property `AGENTS.md` requires of `shared/` and `cpu/`.

**`npm run test:gpu`** — the fifteen kernel checks through Dawn, and
`test:gpu:page` the same fifteen in a real headless Chrome. Needs a WebGPU
device.

**`npm run test:slow`** — about nine minutes, needs a GPU. The checks that have
to integrate for a while before they mean anything: the NPT unit cell read back
by MDAnalysis, the reported temperature against its setpoint at 1, 2 and 4 fs,
the energy drift's timestep scaling, and the live metrics against MDAnalysis.
`npm run test:page:all` drives the nine browser lanes.

The GPU lanes can run in CI too, on a machine that has a GPU:
`tools/setup-gpu-runner.sh` registers one as a self-hosted runner and
`.github/workflows/gpu.yml` drives the three lanes on it, nightly and on demand.

🔴 **AND THAT WORKFLOW HAS NO `pull_request` TRIGGER, WHICH IS THE WHOLE
SECURITY DESIGN.** This repository is public, and a workflow is code: were a
fork's pull request able to reach a self-hosted runner, anyone who can open one
could run whatever they liked on the machine it sits on. GitHub's own guidance
is to pair self-hosted runners with private repositories only. Triggering on a
nightly schedule and manual dispatch only removes the path entirely, and the
installer **refuses to run** if that ever stops being true. It does not run on
push either, which is a cost decision rather than a security one: the lanes are
about eleven and a half minutes of a real GPU, so they run overnight and when
`gh workflow run gpu` asks. Worth
turning on either way: Settings → Actions → General → "Require approval for all
external contributors".

🔴 **A GREEN TICK ON THE HOSTED LANE COVERS LESS THAN HALF THE SUITE, AND THE
WORKFLOW SAYS SO.** GitHub's hosted runners have no GPU, so every kernel, every page lane and
every long integration is outside it. What CI does catch is the class of defect
that has broken this repository most often — a backtick inside a WGSL template
literal, which stops a file parsing and has happened seven times: `npm test`
walks the whole tree with `node --check`, so it is caught in seconds instead of
by a confusing failure in a lane someone has to remember to run.

```bash
npm run check:openmm      # per-term host energies and forces against OpenMM
npm run check:gradients   # every analytic force against a numerical gradient
npm test                  # the host suite
npm run test:gpu          # all fifteen kernel checks, through Dawn
npm run test:gpu:page     # the same fifteen, in a real headless Chrome
npm run test:gpu:erfc     # the f32 erfc floor the Coulomb tolerance is derived from
npm run fit:erfc          # refit the ten erfc coefficients the kernel ships
npm run check:mdanalysis  # the live metrics against MDAnalysis, on a DCD this wrote
node tools/run-reference-md.mjs 200    # a short simulation on the host oracle
npm run run:gpu -- --steps=2000       # a real GPU run, writing /tmp/rainmd-run.dcd
npm run test:page:simulate            # drive a GPU run through the UI in Chrome
npm run test:page:panels              # photograph the six live panels in Chrome
```

`npm test` includes the one gate that is pure text and still catches a whole
class of outage: `web/app.js` has top-level side effects, so a single
`element("…")` naming a control `index.html` no longer has throws *during module
evaluation* and silently abandons the rest of the file — handlers unregistered,
debug handle unassigned, and a page that still looks fine because the device
panel was filled by an earlier statement. The test diffs the two files.

The GPU checks are layered so a failure localises itself:

| | |
|---|---|
| `test:gpu:bonded` | bonds, angles, torsions against the host reference |
| `test:gpu:fft` | the WGSL FFT against a naive DFT, on random data |
| `test:gpu:pme` | spread grid, reciprocal energy and forces |
| `test:gpu:nonbonded` | the cell list as a partition, the neighbour list as a *set*, then the forces |
| `test:gpu:forces` | **everything composed, against OpenMM** |
| `test:gpu:integrator` | one step against the host; then constraint geometry, energy conservation and the thermostat, on the device alone |
| `test:gpu:minimiser` | monotonicity, constraints, and whether dynamics runs from the result |
| `test:gpu:barostat` | the energy at a forced volume scale against OpenMM, then whether the sampler moves the box |

The oracle is OpenMM itself, built with the same arguments the notebooks pass to
`createSystem` — PME, a 1.0 nm cutoff, `HBonds`, rigid water. Regenerate it
with:

```bash
export PATH=/path/to/ambertools/bin:$PATH
tools/oracle/make_fixtures.sh
python3 tools/oracle/dump_openmm_reference.py \
    --prmtop test/fixtures/ala-wat.prmtop \
    --inpcrd test/fixtures/ala-wat.inpcrd \
    --out    test/fixtures/ala-wat-pme.json \
    --nonbonded PME --constraints HBonds --full-forces
```

That script also runs in Colab, so you can dump a reference for **your own**
system and check this engine against it before trusting it with a long run.

## How it is laid out

```
shared/     device-agnostic: the AMBER parser, topology, PME setup, units
cpu/        reference implementations — the oracle, not dead weight
webgpu/     runtime (device, allocator, pipeline cache) and WGSL kernels
web/        the page
tools/      oracles, differential checks, the dev server
docs/       ARCHITECTURE.md is the reverse-engineering result
```

`shared <- cpu <- webgpu`, and a kernel shares its reference's filename. This is
LocalFold's layout and it is deliberate: the CPU file next to each kernel is
what the kernel is tested against.

## Credit

The method, the pipeline and the reason this exists are
**[Making it rain: cloud-based molecular simulations for everyone](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jcim.1c00998)**
by **Pablo R. Arantes**, **Marcelo D. Polêto**, **Conrado Pedebos** and
**Rodrigo Ligabue-Braun**. The two notebooks in this repository's parent
directory are the specification this port follows.

The architecture is **[LocalFold](https://github.com/sokrypton/localfold)** by
Sergey Ovchinnikov and contributors, itself a fork of
**[AlphaFold2 WebGPU](https://github.com/martin-steinegger/alphafold2-webgpu)**
by Martin Steinegger — which is where running a scientific model in a browser on
WebGPU started. Nothing in `webgpu/runtime/` would be the shape it is without
reading theirs; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` says which eight things were taken and
why.

The live-analysis design is **[JIGGLE](https://github.com/BioCoder007/JIGGLE)**
by BioCoder007 — a Qt desktop application that runs OpenMM locally and reports
while the simulation runs. The incremental RMSF, the fit-on-receptor RMSD and
the rule that the viewer and the metrics both exclude solvent are all theirs.

The physics is **[OpenMM](https://openmm.org/)**, which is both what the
notebooks run and the oracle every force term here is checked against. The
analysis is additionally cross-checked against
**[MDAnalysis](https://www.mdanalysis.org/)**. The force
field is AMBER's, via **[AmberTools](https://ambermd.org/AmberTools.php)**.

> Eastman P, Swails J, Chodera JD, et al. OpenMM 7: Rapid development of high
> performance algorithms for molecular dynamics. *PLoS Comput Biol* 13(7):
> e1005659 (2017).

## License

MIT for the code; see `LICENSE`. Force-field parameters are not covered by it —
AMBER's remain under their own terms, and this repository redistributes none of
them beyond the small test systems under `test/fixtures/`, every one of which
`tools/oracle/make_fixtures.sh` builds from a local AmberTools — with two
caveats it would be dishonest to leave out. The two solvated systems place their
ions with `addIonsRand`, so a rebuild is an *equivalent* system rather than a
byte-identical one; every other fixture rebuilds byte-for-byte apart from the
`%VERSION` date stamp. And `two-body.prmtop` is **not** built by that script: its
recipe was never recorded and could not be recovered, so it is listed as a known
exception in `test/amber-parse.test.js`, which fails if that list and the
directory ever disagree.

## 是什么

Prolix 是一个基于 JAX 的蛋白质物理与分子动力学（MD）模拟专用库，旨在为 JAX 生态提供高效的力场、能量计算和 MD 积分器实现。它目前处于积极开发阶段，尚未用于生产环境。

## 亮点

- **JAX 原生集成**：利用 JAX 的自动微分和 GPU/TPU 加速，实现可微分的 MD 模拟。
- **隐式溶剂模型**：实现了 Generalized Born（GBSA）模型，采用 OBC2 参数，支持隐式溶剂模拟。
- **力场支持**：支持 AMBER 力场（ff14SB、ff19SB），并包含 CMAP 校正，提高二面角精度。
- **模块化设计**：与 proxide 库（蛋白质 I/O 和力场加载）解耦，便于替换和扩展。
- **测试与开发工具**：提供 pytest 测试框架，支持 smoke 测试、OpenMM 对比测试，以及 ruff/pyright 代码质量检查。

## 为何对本课题有用

Prolix 直接面向蛋白质结构 × AI/计算模拟课题，其价值在于：

- **可微分的 MD 模拟**：基于 JAX 的力场和积分器支持端到端反向传播，可用于训练基于物理的神经网络或进行结构-能量联合优化。
- **隐式溶剂模型**：GBSA 模型可加速构象采样，避免显式水分子计算，适合大规模构象搜索。
- **力场与 AI 结合**：支持 AMBER 力场，可作为 AI 预测结构的物理约束或能量函数，用于结构精修或构象生成。
- **与 JAX 生态兼容**：可无缝集成到 JAX-based 的深度学习 pipeline 中，用于蛋白质结构预测、构象生成或分子对接的评分函数。

## 怎么用

- **安装**：需先安装 proxide，再安装 prolix。推荐从 GitHub 安装：
  ```bash
  pip install "git+https://github.com/maraxen/proxide.git@main"
  pip install "git+https://github.com/maraxen/prolix.git@main"
  ```
  或从源码安装：`pip install .`，开发模式：`pip install -e ".[dev]"`。
- **主入口**：示例代码位于 README，核心模块为 `prolix.physics.simulate`（MD 模拟）和 `prolix.physics.system`（能量函数）。
- **输入/输出**：输入为 PDB 文件（通过 proxide 加载），输出为模拟轨迹或能量值。
- **GPU 加速**：依赖 JAX，支持 GPU/TPU，需安装相应 JAX 版本（如 `jax[cuda12]`）。
- **测试**：运行 `pytest` 执行全部测试，`pytest -m smoke` 运行快速冒烟测试。

## 核心 idea

Prolix 的核心方法学在于将蛋白质力场（AMBER）和隐式溶剂模型（GBSA）完全实现在 JAX 中，从而利用 JAX 的自动微分和向量化能力，使 MD 模拟成为可微分的计算图。这使得能量函数和模拟轨迹可以反向传播梯度，为 AI 驱动的结构优化和构象采样提供了物理基础。

## 可搬移点

- **力场能量函数**：`prolix.physics.system.make_energy_fn` 可被解耦，作为自定义 pipeline 中的可微能量项，用于结构预测或构象生成。
- **隐式溶剂模型**：GBSA/OBC2 实现可移植到其他 JAX-based 模拟框架，加速构象采样。
- **MD 积分器**：`prolix.physics.simulate.run_simulation` 支持自定义热浴和积分器，可替换为其他采样算法（如 Langevin 动力学）。
- **License**：MIT，允许自由使用和修改，但需确认具体版本。

（注：README 未提供具体模块文件路径，以上基于文档描述。）
readme:
# Prolix

**Prolix** is a specialized library for Protein Physics and molecular dynamics simulations in JAX. It provides efficient implementations of force fields, energy calculations, and MD integrations for the JAX ecosystem.

**NOTE**: This is a work-in-progress library and is not yet ready for production use. It is currently in active development and subject to change.

## Features

- **JAX MD Integration**: Seamless bridging between protein force fields and JAX MD simulations
- **Implicit Solvent**: Generalized Born (GBSA) implementation with OBC2 model
- **Force Fields**: Support for AMBER force fields (ff14SB, ff19SB) with CMAP corrections
- **Energy Calculations**: Bond, angle, torsion, and non-bonded energy terms
- **MD Simulations**: Stable molecular dynamics with customizable thermostats and integrators

## Installation

### From GitHub (Recommended)

**Prolix** depends on **proxide** (protein I/O and force fields). Install `proxide` first, then `prolix`:

```bash
pip install "git+https://github.com/maraxen/proxide.git@main"
pip install "git+https://github.com/maraxen/prolix.git@main"
```

If `proxide` is already on PyPI for your platform, `pip install "git+https://github.com/maraxen/prolix.git@main"` may resolve it automatically; otherwise use the two-step order above (proxide uses a Rust/`maturin` build).

### From Source

To install Prolix from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/maraxen/prolix.git
cd prolix
pip install .
```

For development installation with test dependencies:

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

Optional OpenMM parity tooling: `pip install -e ".[dev,openmm]"` (requires a compatible PyPI wheel for your platform; see `pyproject.toml`).

### UV workspace (editable proxide)

`proxide` is pinned for UV as a workspace member. With sibling checkouts `…/prolix` and `…/proxide`, install from their parent (see `workspace/README.md`):

```bash
# from the prolix repo root; ../proxide must exist
bash scripts/sync_workspace_lock.sh
cd .. && uv sync --extra cuda --extra dev --package prolix
```

After changing dependencies in `pyproject.toml`, run `bash scripts/sync_workspace_lock.sh` again and commit `workspace/uv.lock`.

## Usage

### Running a Simple MD Simulation

```python
from proxide.io.parsing import load_structure
from proxide.physics.force_fields import load_force_field
from prolix.physics.simulate import run_simulation

protein = load_structure("protein.pdb")
ff = load_force_field("path/to/ff19SB.eqx")
# Combine the structure and force field into system parameters (see docs / tutorials), then:
# final_positions = run_simulation(system_params, protein.coord, temperature=300.0)
```

### Computing Energy

```python
from jax_md import space
from prolix.physics import system

# Create energy function
displacement_fn, _ = space.free()
energy_fn = system.make_energy_fn(
    displacement_fn=displacement_fn,
    system_params=params,
    implicit_solvent=True
)

# Compute energy
energy = energy_fn(positions)
```

## Development

### Running Tests

Run the full test suite:

```bash
pytest
```

Run fast "smoke" tests to verify core functionality:

```bash
pytest -m smoke
```

### Linting and Typing

Check code quality:

```bash
ruff check .
pyright
```

## Dependencies

Prolix depends on:

- **proxide**: Protein I/O, parsing, and force field loading
- **jax-md**: Molecular dynamics primitives
- **jax**: Automatic differentiation and accelerators
- **equinox**: Modules and serialization

## License

MIT License - see LICENSE file for details.

card:
## 是什么

这是一个基于图神经网络（GNN）的蛋白质功能预测工具，专门用于从实验解析的3D蛋白质结构中预测多标签酶学委员会（EC）催化功能。它构建了残基级别的3D接触图，并评估了多种模型架构（1D序列CNN、接触图卷积网络GCN、边条件图注意力网络GAT），在严格的<30%序列同源性划分下进行基准测试。

## 亮点

- **严格的同源性划分**：采用RCSB 30%序列同一性聚类，确保训练/验证/测试集无重叠，评估结果更具泛化性。
- **多模型对比**：同时实现并比较了序列基线（1D CNN）和两种图模型（GCN、GAT），便于公平评估3D结构信息的增益。
- **丰富的特征工程**：节点特征包含20种氨基酸one-hot和6个主链伪二面角正弦/余弦，边特征包含16个高斯径向基距离bin和归一化序列间隔，充分编码几何与序列信息。
- **端到端流程**：从数据下载、图构建、训练、评估到可视化，提供完整脚本和配置，易于复现。
- **混合精度训练**：支持PyTorch AMP（bfloat16），在RTX 5090上高效训练。

## 为何对本课题有用

该仓库直接属于蛋白质结构×AI/计算模拟课题方向，其核心价值在于：
- **结构-功能关系建模**：展示了如何将3D原子坐标转化为残基接触图，并利用GNN学习催化活性位点的几何基序，这对于理解蛋白质结构与功能的关系至关重要。
- **可迁移的图构建方法**：其图构建逻辑（Cα距离、k-NN、RBF边特征）可直接用于其他结构预测或构象采样任务，例如将预测的结构转换为图表示以进行下游功能或相互作用预测。
- **多标签分类框架**：EC预测的多标签分类框架可迁移至其他蛋白质功能注释任务（如GO预测），或用于评估生成结构的生物学有效性。
- **同源性划分策略**：严格的同源性划分方法可借鉴于任何蛋白质机器学习任务，以避免数据泄漏，提高模型泛化能力。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：`scripts/train.py`（训练）、`scripts/predict.py`（推理）、`scripts/download_data.py`（数据下载）、`scripts/make_figures.py`（可视化）。
- **安装**：使用`environment.yml`创建conda环境，然后`pip install -e .`。
- **依赖**：见`pyproject.toml`，核心依赖为PyTorch、numpy、pandas、scipy、scikit-learn、biopython、umap-learn、matplotlib、seaborn、pyyaml、tqdm。
- **数据格式**：输入为PDB结构（通过CATH 4.2坐标），输出为EC类别概率。数据文件为`ec_pdb_splits.csv`和`ec_pdb_splits.npz`，包含序列、结构、标签和划分信息。
- **测试**：运行`pytest tests/ -v`，有9个单元测试，覆盖数据、模型和评估。
- **GPU需求**：需要GPU（推荐RTX 5090级别）以加速训练，但推理可在CPU上运行。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学洞察在于：**将蛋白质的3D结构编码为残基接触图，并通过边条件图注意力机制动态加权残基间相互作用，从而直接学习催化活性位点的几何基序，而非依赖序列同源性**。这种方法能够捕捉序列发散但结构收敛的蛋白质之间的功能相似性，从而在严格的同源性划分下仍能取得优于序列基线的性能。

## 可搬移点

- **图构建模块**（`src/protgnn/data/graph_builder.py`）：最值得解耦，其Cα距离计算、k-NN邻居选择、RBF边特征生成可独立用于任何蛋白质结构图构建任务，例如将AlphaFold预测的结构转换为图输入。
- **特征工程**（`src/protgnn/data/constants.py`）：节点和边特征定义可复用，特别是伪二面角编码和RBF距离bin，可迁移至其他结构感知模型。
- **评估指标**（`src/protgnn/evaluation/metrics.py`）：多标签F1、MCC、AUPR、LRAP的实现可直接用于其他多标签蛋白质功能预测任务。
- **同源性划分逻辑**（`scripts/download_data.py`）：基于RCSB聚类划分数据集的方法可迁移至任何蛋白质机器学习项目，确保评估严谨性。
- **License**：MIT许可证，允许自由使用和修改，但需确认具体版本。

该仓库的模块化设计（数据、模型、训练、评估分离）使其易于逐步替换和集成到自定义Pipeline中，例如替换模型架构或特征提取层。

# Protein Function Prediction via Graph Neural Networks on 3D Residue Graphs

[![Python 3.11](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
[![PyTorch 2.5+](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-2.5%2B-ee4c2c.svg)](https://pytorch.org/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![Code Style: Ruff](https://img.shields.io/badge/code%20style-ruff-000000.svg)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff)

> **Predicting multi-label Enzyme Commission (EC) catalytic function from experimental 3D protein structures using Contact Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) and Edge-Conditioned Graph Attention Networks (GAT) evaluated under strict <30% sequence identity homology partitioning.**

---

## 🔬 Scientific Abstract & Problem Statement

Accurate annotation of enzyme catalytic function directly from 3D atomic coordinates is a central challenge in structural biology, protein engineering, and functional genomics. While sequence-based models often fail when functional convergence occurs between structurally homologous yet sequence-divergent proteins, **Graph Neural Networks (GNNs)** operating on residue-level 3D spatial contact networks can directly learn catalytic active-site geometric motifs.

This project implements an end-to-end geometric deep learning framework benchmarked on **4,709 real experimental crystal enzyme chains** combining **CATH 4.2 coordinates**, **RCSB GraphQL `rcsb_ec_lineage` annotations**, and **RCSB 30% sequence-identity clusters**:
1. **Geometric Graph Featurization**: 3D $C_\alpha$ backbone trajectories (chains 40–500 aa with $\ge 85\%$ resolved crystal density) are converted into spatial contact graphs ($r \le 10.0$ Å, $k$-NN $k \le 30$) with 26-dimensional node features (20 amino acid one-hot + 6 backbone pseudo-dihedral $\sin/\cos$ angles) and 17-dimensional edge attributes (16 Gaussian Radial Basis Function distance bins + normalized sequence separation).
2. **Architectures Evaluated**:
   - **1D Dilated Sequence CNN**: Baseline operating purely on primary sequence without 3D geometric awareness.
   - **Contact Graph Convolutional Network (GCN)**: Spatial message passing with edge feature modulation and global attention pooling.
   - **Edge-Conditioned Graph Attention Network (GAT)**: Multi-head attention dynamically weighting residue contacts and active-site topology.
3. **Rigorous Homology Partitioning**: Evaluated on **688 held-out test chains** partitioned strictly at **<30% sequence identity** (`3,578 train / 443 val / 688 test`; `0` cluster overlap) across the Top-25 populated fine-grained EC subclasses spanning EC 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6.

---

## 📊 Benchmark Results (<30% Sequence Identity Test Set)

All models evaluated on the held-out test split of **688 experimental crystal chains** across **25 fine-grained Enzyme Commission subclasses**:

| Model Architecture | Graph Modality | Macro-F1 | Micro-F1 | Macro-MCC | Macro-AUPR | LRAP |
|:---|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **1D Dilated CNN Baseline** | 1D Primary Sequence | 0.1322 | 0.1652 | 0.0987 | 0.1196 | 0.3566 |
| **Contact GCN** | 3D Residue Contact Graph | 0.1825 | 0.1930 | 0.1565 | 0.1924 | 0.4323 |
| **Edge-Conditioned GAT** | 3D Attentive Contact Graph | **0.2199** | **0.2227** | **0.2052** | **0.2230** | **0.4510** |

*Hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (32 GB VRAM), PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128 with mixed precision (AMP bfloat16).*

---

## 📈 Publication-Quality Visualizations

### Figure 1: EC Hierarchy & Multi-Label Class Distribution
![Figure 1: EC Hierarchy](reports/figures/01_ec_hierarchy_and_distribution.png)
*Panel A: Distribution across EC divisions (`4,709` chains across Oxidoreductases, Transferases, Hydrolases, Lyases, Ligases). Panel B: Frequency ranking of 25 benchmark fine-grained EC subclasses. Panel C: Multi-function co-occurrence conditional probability matrix $P(\text{Column} \mid \text{Row})\%$ (e.g., 22% co-occurrence between EC 2.7.11 and EC 2.7.1).*

---

## 是什么

这是一个复现 2024 年 Zhang 等人研究论文（*Machine-learning-based Structural Analysis of Interactions between Antibodies and Antigens*）的完整全栈机器学习应用。它从抗体-抗原复合物结构（PDB/CIF）中提取 5 Å 侧链重原子接触，构建 20×20 或 20×21 的接触矩阵，并用 CNN 对复合物进行分类或分析，同时提供 FastAPI 后端和前端界面。

## 亮点

- **精确复现论文方法**：严格遵循论文中的 5 Å 侧链重原子接触定义、上下三角矩阵构建、逐复合物 min-max 归一化，并修复了原论文参考实现中 MaxPooling 导致维度塌缩的 bug（20×20 → 128 维而非 288 维）。
- **严谨的防泄漏数据划分**：基于 SAbDab 的 `ab_ag_cluster` 进行 group-splitting，确保测试集与训练/验证集在抗体-抗原簇和 PDB 层面零重叠。
- **健壮的结构解析**：支持 .cif/.mmcif/.pdb，自动从 RCSB 下载缺失结构，保留原始晶体学编号和插入码，不硬编码链 ID，通过全局比对将 SAbDab IMGT 编号映射到结构残基。
- **确定性输出**：所有矩阵生成、哈希、数据集划分均具有确定性，便于复现和审计。
- **完整测试套件**：49 个测试覆盖环境、结构解析、接触提取、数据集构建、模型训练和推理，全部通过。

## 为何对本课题有用

该仓库直接属于“蛋白质结构 × AI/计算模拟”课题方向，尤其聚焦于抗体-抗原相互作用的结构分析。它提供了从结构文件到 CNN 输入张量的完整、可复现的流水线，可直接用于：
- 抗体-抗原结合界面残基的自动识别和特征化。
- 基于接触矩阵的蛋白-蛋白相互作用（PPI）分类或预测。
- 作为结构特征提取模块，可迁移到其他蛋白复合物（如酶-底物、受体-配体）的相互作用分析。
- 其防泄漏数据划分方法对任何基于结构数据的机器学习任务都有借鉴价值。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：后端 API 入口为 `backend/app/main.py`（FastAPI），前端为 `frontend/index.html`。
- **安装依赖**：`pip install -r backend/requirements.txt`（包含 biopython, numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn, tensorflow, keras, fastapi, uvicorn, pydantic, requests, pytest, httpx）。
- **运行测试**：`pytest backend/tests/` 可运行全部 49 个测试，验证环境、结构解析、接触提取、数据集构建和模型训练。
- **命令行工具**：
  - `python scripts/analyze_structure.py 1EJO --phase structure` 查看结构解析和链识别。
  - `python scripts/analyze_structure.py 1EJO --phase matrix -v` 查看接触矩阵。
  - `python scripts/analyze_structure.py 1EJO --export` 导出 .npy 和 .csv 矩阵。
  - `python scripts/build_dataset.py --val-fraction 0.20 --seed 42 --unseen-pdb 1A3R` 构建数据集并生成划分。
- **数据格式**：输入为 PDB/CIF 结构文件（本地缓存或自动下载），元数据来自 `data/abdb/abag_split.csv`（包含 IMGT 编号、CDR 范围、链 ID）。输出为 20×20 或 20×21 的 numpy 数组，以及 CSV 清单。
- **需要 GPU**：训练 CNN 时建议使用 GPU 加速，但 CPU 也可运行小规模测试。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学洞察在于：**将抗体-抗原界面接触信息编码为 20×20 的氨基酸对频率矩阵，并通过巧妙的上下三角拼接和逐行过滤，构造出 20×21 的 CNN 输入张量，从而在保持生物学可解释性的同时，满足 CNN 对固定尺寸输入的要求。** 这一设计避免了直接使用原子坐标或距离图，而是将接触频率转化为图像-like 特征，使得 CNN 能够捕捉氨基酸类型间的相互作用模式，且每个复合物独立归一化，保证了跨复合物的可比性。

## 可搬移点

- **接触提取模块**（`backend/app/structure/contacts.py`）：可独立解耦，用于任何蛋白-蛋白复合物的界面接触分析，只需提供结构文件和链 ID。
- **矩阵构建与归一化**（`backend/app/structure/representation.py`）：可移植到其他基于接触矩阵的机器学习任务，支持自定义氨基酸映射和归一化策略。
- **防泄漏数据划分**（`backend/app/datasets/splitting.py`）：可复用于任何需要按簇划分的数据集构建，避免训练/测试泄漏。
- **CNN 架构**（`backend/app/ml/cnn.py`）：可修改输入维度后用于其他 2D 特征图分类任务。
- **License**：README 未说明，需确认。

# ANTIBODY–ANTIGEN INTERACTION ANALYZER V2
## Research Paper Reproduction + Full-Stack ML Application
**Reference Study**: *"Machine-learning-based Structural Analysis of Interactions between Antibodies and Antigens"* — Grace Zhang, Zhaoqian Su, Tom Zhang, Yinghao Wu (2024, *BioSystems* 243:105264; bioRxiv: 10.1101/2023.12.06.570397).

---

## 1. Project Overview & Scientific Source of Truth

This project reproduces the core methodology from Zhang et al. (2024) to computationally analyze structural interaction patterns at antibody-antigen interfaces and evaluate them against general protein-protein interactions (PPI) using a convolutional neural network (CNN).

### Key Scientific Principles
1. **Intermolecular Contacts (5 Å side-chain heavy atoms)**:
   - Identify which residues are on the interaction interface (antibody CDR residues ↔ antigen residues).
2. **Intramolecular Contacts (5 Å side-chain heavy atoms)**:
   - Calculate internal contacts **between** interface residues within the antigen (upper diagonal).
   - Calculate internal contacts **between** interface residues within the antibody CDRs (lower diagonal).
   - Intermolecular contacts are **never** placed directly into the 20×20 matrix.
3. **Per-Complex Normalization**:
   - Each complex is individually min-max normalized between 0 and 1.
4. **CNN Architecture & 288-Dimensional Tensor**:
   - 3× Conv2D(32 filters, 3×3 kernel, ReLU, padding='same') followed by MaxPooling2D((2,2), padding='same').
   - Produces a feature map of shape `(3, 3, 32)` which flattens to **exactly 288 dimensions**.
   - Dense(512) → Dense(64) → Dense(1, sigmoid).

---

## 2. Phase 1 Audit & Scientific Findings

### Dataset Discovery & Schema
| Dataset | Source | Total Items | Format & Schema |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AbDb / SAbDab** | AbDb / SAbDab export | 1,215 complexes (`AbDb_list.dat`) | PDB/CIF structures; `abag_split.csv` containing IMGT numbering, CDR H1-H3 & L1-L3 ranges, heavy/light chain IDs, and antigen chain IDs. |
| **3did General PPI** | 3did Database | 4,144 non-redundant pairs (`pdb_4960list.txt`) | Tab-delimited: `Index PDB Chain1 Start1 End1 Chain2 Start2 End2` (3,218 inter-chain pairs used in Test 1). |

### 288-Dimensional Bottleneck Resolution
The paper specifies a 288-dimensional flattened representation. Our mathematical and code audit of the author's reference notebook revealed:
- When using `MaxPooling2D((2, 2))` with default `padding='valid'`, the output dimensions collapse: `(20, 20) -> (10, 10) -> (5, 5) -> (2, 2)`, yielding `2 * 2 * 32 = 128` dimensions (the flaw in the previous reference implementation).
- When using `MaxPooling2D((2, 2), padding='same')`, the odd spatial dimension is preserved: `ceil(5/2) = 3`, yielding `3 * 3 * 32 = 288` dimensions.
- Test `backend/tests/test_phase1_environment.py::test_cnn_architecture_produces_exact_288_dimensions` verified this behavior.

---

## 5. Phase 2 Structure Parsing & Entity Identification Architecture

### Supported Formats & Sources
- Formats: `.cif`, `.mmcif`, `.pdb`
- Retrieval: Local cache in `data/structures/`, with automated fallback retrieval from RCSB PDB (`https://files.rcsb.org/download/{pdb_id}.cif`).

### Chain & Entity Identification Method
- **Antibody Heavy and Light Chains**: Identified from `abag_split.csv` (`Hchain`, `Lchain`) with recorded biological evidence. Avoids hardcoded assumptions (e.g. In `1NBZ` and `1DQJ`, Heavy chain is `B` and Light chain is `A`).
- **Antigen Chains**: Sourced from `agchains` metadata, handling multi-chain antigens (e.g. `A/B`).
- **Residue Numbering & Identity**: Preserves original crystallographic residue numbering (e.g. `1EJO` Chain H numbered in the 2500s) and insertion codes without arbitrary renumbering.
- **CDR Identification**: Aligns structural standard residues against SAbDab IMGT numbering sequences using global pairwise alignment. Mapped residues are extracted within IMGT standard intervals:
  - CDR1: 27–38
  - CDR2: 56–65
  - CDR3: 105–117
  Mapped CDR sequences are cross-validated against expected sequences (`CDRH1..3`, `CDRL1..3`).

### Diagnostic CLI
Run the diagnostic tool for any structure:
```bash
# Structure and entity diagnostics (Phase 2)
python scripts/analyze_structure.py 1EJO --phase structure

# Matrix and contact diagnostics (Phase 3)
python scripts/analyze_structure.py 1EJO --phase matrix -v

# Run full diagnostic and export matrix files (.npy and .csv)
python scripts/analyze_structure.py 1EJO --export
```

---

## 6. Phase 3 5 Å Contact Extraction & Representation Architecture

### Scientific Methodology
1. **Side-Chain Heavy Atom Filtering**:
   - Strictly excludes backbone atoms: `N`, `CA`, `C`, `O`, `OXT`.
   - Strictly excludes hydrogen atoms: element `H` or names starting with `H`.
   - Residues without side-chain heavy atoms (e.g. standard Glycine) produce no side-chain contacts.
2. **Intermolecular Contacts (<= 5.0 Å Cutoff)**:
   - Uses `scipy.spatial.cKDTree` for spatial neighbor search between antibody side-chain heavy atoms and antigen side-chain heavy atoms.
   - Identifies interface residues:
     - All antibody interface residues.
     - CDR interface residues (subset belonging to IMGT CDR H1–H3 or L1–L3).
     - Framework interface residues.
     - Antigen interface residues (supporting multi-chain antigens).
3. **Intramolecular Interface Contacts**:
   - **Antigen**: Contacts calculated strictly among antigen interface residues.
   - **Antibody**: Contacts calculated strictly among antibody CDR interface residues.
   - **No Atom-Pair Multiplicity Inflation**: Each contacting residue pair $(r_1, r_2)$ with $r_1 \neq r_2$ is counted exactly once, matching Biopython's `NeighborSearch.search_all(5, level='R')` in author's reference notebook `part1.ipynb`.
4. **Deterministic Amino Acid Mapping**:
   - 20 standard amino acids alphabetized by 3-letter code:
     `ALA (0), ARG (1), ASN (2), ASP (3), CYS (4), GLN (5), GLU (6), GLY (7), HIS (8), ILE (9), LEU (10), LYS (11), MET (12), PHE (13), PRO (14), SER (15), THR (16), TRP (17), TYR (18), VAL (19)`.
   - Corresponding 1-letter codes: `A, R, N, D, C, Q, E, G, H, I, L, K, M, F, P, S, T, W, Y, V`.
5. **Upper / Lower Triangle Construction & Orientation**:
   - Antigen intramolecular pair frequencies populate the upper triangle (`r <= c`), with below-diagonal as `NaN`.
   - Antibody CDR intramolecular pair frequencies populate the upper triangle of the antibody chart, with below-diagonal as `NaN`.
   - Diagonal entries represent contacts between different residues of the same amino-acid type (e.g. `TYR` ↔ `TYR`).
6. **Per-Complex Min-Max Normalization**:
   - Formula: $x' = \frac{x - \text{nanmin}(x)}{\text{nanmax}(x) - \text{nanmin}(x)}$
   - Evaluated independently per complex (never global across the dataset).
   - Safe zero-range handling: If $\text{nanmax} = \text{nanmin}$ (e.g. empty or constant), populates with $0.0$ to prevent division by zero or NaN generation.
7. **Matrix Dimensions (20×20 vs 20×21)**:
   - **Canonical Scientific Representation `(20, 20)`**: Upper triangle holds antigen normalized contacts; lower triangle holds antibody CDR normalized contacts.
   - **Author's CNN Input Tensor `(20, 21)`**: Flipping the antibody upper triangle (`np.flip(Ab)`) yields $r + 1$ non-NaN values in row $r$; concatenating with antigen upper triangle row $r$ ($20 - r$ non-NaN values) and filtering out NaNs yields exactly $21$ values per row for all $20$ rows. Input shape to CNN is `(20, 21, 1)`.
   - Both representations are computed, tested, and exported.

## 7. Phase 4 Dataset Construction & Leakage-Safe Validation

### Dataset Architecture & Filtering Pipeline
1. **Metadata Source**:
   - `data/abdb/abag_split.csv`: 15,641 instances representing 8,641 unique PDB complexes with SAbDab IMGT numbering, sequence clusters (`ab_cluster`, `agclusters`, `ab_ag_cluster`), and official benchmark split (`ab_ag_split`).
2. **Deterministic Rejection Categorization**:
   - Samples undergo strict biological and structural validation. No zero-matrix fallbacks or synthetic perturbations are allowed.
   - Rejection categories:
     - `missing_pdb_id`
     - `missing_structure`
     - `structure_parse_error`
     - `missing_antibody_metadata`
     - `missing_antigen_metadata` (e.g. unbound structures or hapten complexes)
     - `cdr_mapping_failure`
     - `no_interface_contacts`
     - `no_valid_representation`
     - `unsupported_structure`
3. **Leakage-Safe Cluster Partitioning**:
   - Preserves SAbDab's official test partition isolated strictly by `ab_ag_cluster`.
   - Sub-partitions training candidates into `train` (~80%) and `validation` (~20%) using group-splitting on `ab_ag_cluster` with fixed seed 42.
   - Zero Ab-Ag cluster overlap and zero PDB overlap between test and train/val sets.
   - The default dataset build targets a 10,000-sample training pool before split assignment, while still honoring the full metadata-driven leakage checks.
4. **Reproducible Storage**:
   - Manifest: `data/processed/dataset_manifest.csv`
   - Rejections: `data/processed/rejected_samples.csv`
   - Split manifests: `data/processed/train.csv`, `data/processed/validation.csv`, `data/processed/test.csv`
   - Author-compatible tensors: `data/processed/representations/<sample_id>.npy` (shape `(20, 21)`).
5. **Unseen Structure Validation**:
   - Structure `1A3R` (not part of the Phase 3 benchmarks) was executed through the identical production pipeline:
     - Heavy: `H`, Light: `L`, Antigen: `['P']`
     - All 6 CDRs matched to coordinates
     - 373 intermolecular contacts, 23 CDR interface residues, 14 Ag interface residues
     - 28 Ab CDR intra contacts, 15 Ag intra contacts
     - Valid (20, 21) tensor, 30 nonzero cells, SHA256: `c422403f6c9c7978...`

### Build Script CLI
```bash
# Build dataset on all cached structures with deterministic splitting
python scripts/build_dataset.py

# Re-run with custom validation fraction or seed
python scripts/build_dataset.py --val-fraction 0.20 --seed 42 --unseen-pdb 1A3R
```

one_liner: MDAnalysis 是分子动力学模拟轨迹分析的核心 Python 库，虽不直接做结构预测或生成，但为蛋白质结构计算（如 MD 模拟后处理、构象分析）提供关键工具，与课题高度相关。
readme:
================================
  MDAnalysis Repository README
================================

|numfocus| 

|build| |cron| |cirruscron| |linters| |cov|

|docs| |devdocs| |discussions|

|pypi| |anaconda| |asv|

MDAnalysis_ is a Python library for the analysis of computer simulations of many-body systems at the molecular scale, spanning use cases from interactions of drugs with proteins to novel materials. It is widely used in the scientific community and is written by scientists for scientists. 

It works with a wide range of popular simulation packages including GROMACS, Amber, NAMD, CHARMM, DL_POLY, HOOMD, LAMMPS and many others — see the lists of supported `trajectory formats`_ and `topology formats`_.
MDAnalysis also includes widely used analysis algorithms in the `MDAnalysis.analysis`_ module.

.. _numfocus-fiscal-sponsor-attribution:

The MDAnalysis project uses an `open governance model`_ and is fiscally sponsored by `NumFOCUS`_. Consider making 
a `tax-deductible donation`_ to help the project pay for developer time, professional services, travel, workshops, and a variety of other needs.

.. image:: https://www.mdanalysis.org/public/images/numfocus-sponsored-small.png
   :alt: NumFOCUS (Fiscally Sponsored Project)
   :target: https://numfocus.org/project/mdanalysis
   :align: center

This project is bound by a `Code of Conduct`_.

|powered_by_MDA|

If you use MDAnalysis_ in your project consider letting your users and the world know about it by displaying the MDAnalysis_ badge! `Embedding code`_ is available for different markups.

Example analysis script
=======================

.. code:: python

   import MDAnalysis as mda

   # Load simulation results with a single line
   u = mda.Universe('topol.tpr','traj.trr')

   # Select atoms
   ag = u.select_atoms('name OH')

   # Atom data made available as Numpy arrays
   ag.positions
   ag.velocities
   ag.forces

   # Iterate through trajectories
   for ts in u.trajectory:
       print(ag.center_of_mass())


Documentation
=============

**New users** should read the `Quickstart Guide`_ and might want to
look at our videos_, in which core developers explain various aspects
of MDAnalysis.

**All users** should read the `User Guide`_.

**Developers** may also want to refer to the `MDAnalysis API docs`_.

A growing number of `tutorials`_ are available that explain how to
conduct RMSD calculations, structural alignment, distance and contact
analysis, and many more.


Installation and availability
=============================

The latest release can be **installed via pip or conda** as
described in the `Installation Quick Start`_.

**Source code** is hosted in a git repository at
https://github.com/MDAnalysis/mdanalysis and is packaged under the
GNU Lesser General Public License, version 3 or any later version (LGPLv3+).
Individual source code components are provided under the
GNU Lesser General Public License, version 2.1 or any later version (LGPLv2.1+).
Please see the file LICENSE_ for more information.


Contributing
============

Please report **bugs** or **enhancement requests** through the `Issue
Tracker`_. Questions can also be asked on `GitHub Discussions`_.

If you are a **new developer** who would like to start contributing to
MDAnalysis get in touch on `GitHub Discussions`_. To set up a
development environment and run the test suite read the `developer
guide`_.


Citation
========

When using MDAnalysis in published work, please cite the following
two papers:

*   R\. J. Gowers, M. Linke, J. Barnoud, T. J. E. Reddy,
    M\. N. Melo, S. L. Seyler, D. L. Dotson, J. Domanski,
    S\. Buchoux, I. M. Kenney, and O. Beckstein. MDAnalysis:
    A Python package for the rapid analysis of molecular
    dynamics simulations. In S. Benthall and S. Rostrup,
    editors, Proceedings of the 15th Python in Science
    Conference, pages 102-109, Austin, TX, 2016. SciPy.
    doi: `10.25080/Majora-629e541a-00e`_    
*   N. Michaud-Agrawal, E. J. Denning, T. B. Woolf,
    and O. Beckstein. MDAnalysis: A Toolkit for the Analysis of Molecular
    Dynamics Simulations. *J. Comput. Chem.* **32** (2011), 2319--2327.
    doi: `10.1002/jcc.21787`_

For citations of included algorithms and sub-modules please see the references_.

## 是什么
SaprotHub 是一个面向蛋白质语言模型（PLM）的开放协作平台，旨在让没有编程或机器学习背景的生物学家也能通过 Colab 笔记本轻松完成 PLM 的微调、预测和模型共享。它基于 SaProt 模型（融合序列与结构 token），并提出了 Open Protein Modeling Consortium (OPMC) 的概念，以促进社区驱动的去中心化模型协作。

## 亮点
- **零门槛使用**：通过 Colab 笔记本（ColabSaprot、ColabSeprot 等）提供交互式界面，无需本地安装或编写代码。
- **轻量级 Adapter 机制**：仅共享和加载小型 Adapter 模块，而非完整模型权重，大幅降低存储和通信成本，便于社区协作。
- **多模型支持**：除 SaProt 外，还支持 ESM1b、ESM2、ProTrek、ProtBERT、ESMC、ESM3 等主流 PLM，覆盖序列和结构感知模型。
- **本地部署支持**：提供 local_server 目录，允许用户在本地服务器上运行 ColabSaprot，便于离线或大规模使用。
- **社区生态**：通过 Slack、微信等渠道建立活跃社区，并鼓励其他 PLM 加入 OPMC，形成开放联盟。

## 为何对本课题有用
SaprotHub 直接服务于蛋白质结构 × AI/计算模拟课题中的**功能预测**和**序列设计**任务。其核心价值在于：
- **结构感知的 SaProt 模型**：将 3Di 结构 token 与氨基酸序列结合，为结构-序列联合建模提供了现成方案，可用于构象相关预测或设计。
- **Adapter 微调范式**：为蛋白质结构预测或构象采样模型提供了一种高效的迁移学习思路——在共享骨干网络上训练轻量 Adapter，可快速适配不同下游任务（如稳定性预测、结合位点预测）。
- **零代码微调流程**：降低了非计算专家参与模型训练的门槛，有助于生物学家快速验证结构-功能假设。
- **多模型集成**：通过 ColabSeprot 等支持多种 PLM，便于对比不同模型在结构相关任务上的表现。

## 怎么用
- **主入口**：Colab 笔记本位于 `colab/` 目录，如 `colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb`（SaProt 35M/650M）、`colab/ColabSeprot.ipynb`（ESM1b/ESM2/ProTrek/ProtBERT）、`colab/ESM-Play-VC.ipynb`（ESMC）、`colab/ESM-Play-V3.ipynb`（ESM3）。
- **本地部署**：参考 `local_server/` 目录，包含 `install.sh`、`run.sh`、`requirements.txt` 等，可部署到本地 Linux/Windows 服务器。
- **依赖**：核心依赖见 `requirements.txt` 和 `pyproject.toml`，包括 torch、transformers、peft、biopython、lmdb 等。
- **数据格式**：支持 CSV 格式的样本数据（见 `upload_files/` 示例），输入为序列（和可选结构），输出为预测标签或数值。
- **GPU 需求**：微调和预测需要 GPU 加速，Colab 提供免费或付费 GPU 资源。
- **调试**：可通过 Colab 笔记本直接运行，或使用 `saprot/scripts/` 下的脚本（如 `training.py`）进行命令行训练。

## 核心 idea
SaprotHub 的核心方法学是**“以 Adapter 为单位的模型共享与协作”**——通过将大型 PLM 视为固定骨干，仅训练和交换轻量 Adapter，从而在保持模型性能的同时，实现低成本的社区化微调与迭代。这一设计借鉴了“嫁接”思想，使得不同研究者可以在同一骨干上贡献各自的任务适配器，形成可组合的模型生态。

## 可搬移点
- **Adapter 微调框架**：`saprot/model/saprot/self_peft/` 下的 PEFT 实现（`peft_model.py`、`mapping.py`、`save_and_load.py`）可被解耦，用于任何基于 transformer 的蛋白质模型（如 ESM、SaProt）的轻量微调，适合移植到自定义结构预测或构象采样 Pipeline。
- **数据预处理模块**：`saprot/data/` 下的 `pdb2feature.py`、`pdb2prosst.py`、`sequence_to_prosst.py` 等，可将 PDB 结构转换为 3Di token 或特征，可直接复用于结构感知的输入构建。
- **模型接口**：`saprot/model/abstract_model.py` 和 `model_interface.py` 提供了统一的模型抽象，便于替换或扩展新的 PLM。
- **License**：README 未明确说明 License，需确认。
