# GeneStructor [![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![R ≥ 4.4](https://img.shields.io/badge/R-%E2%89%A54.4-276DC3.svg)](https://www.r-project.org/) [![Data on Zenodo](https://img.shields.io/badge/data-10.5281%2Fzenodo.23880730-1682D4.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23880730) **Rank the gene models at a locus by the protein structures they encode.** GeneStructor scores every gene model (transcript) at a gene locus using the predicted structure of the protein it encodes, how well the folded structure matches known protein structures, and sequence-based evidence. An ensemble of logistic regression models, trained on manually curated rice gene models, combines this evidence into one score per gene model, and the gene models at each locus are ranked by that score. It was developed to resolve conflicting gene models in the rice (*Oryza sativa*) Nipponbare reference genome, where the RAP-DB, RGAP (MSU) and Gramene annotations frequently disagree, and is designed to be adaptable to other species with competing gene models or alternative isoforms. **Contact:** Eshan Sharma and Andrew R. Jones ([PGB-LIV](https://github.com/PGB-LIV)). Please report problems on the [issue tracker](https://github.com/PGB-LIV/GeneStructor/issues). ## Contents - [How GeneStructor works](#how-genestructor-works) - [Benchmark on rice](#benchmark-on-rice) - [Installation](#installation) - [Quick start: from .pdb files to ranked gene models](#quick-start-from-pdb-files-to-ranked-gene-models) - [Running on your own gene models](#running-on-your-own-gene-models) - [Output](#output) - [Interpreting the results](#interpreting-the-results) - [Repository layout](#repository-layout) - [Data availability](#data-availability) - [Citation and license](#citation-and-license) ## How GeneStructor works ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Gene models
(merged GFF3)"] --> B["Protein sequences
(FASTA)"] B --> C["Structure prediction
AlphaFold2 or Protenix-mini
(.pdb / .cif)"] C --> D["pLDDT counts
structure_metrics.R"] C --> E["Foldseek search
PDB + AlphaFold/Swiss-Prot"] B --> F["InterProScan"] B --> G["PSAURON"] D & E & F & G --> H["Metrics table
(build_metrics_table.R)"] H --> I["logistic regression models
"] I --> J["Ranked gene models per locus
(rank_isoforms.R)"] ``` 1. **Collect the gene models.** Gene models from one or more annotations are merged so that every transcript belongs to a parent gene locus, and the encoded protein sequences are extracted. 2. **Compute the evidence.** Each protein is folded with AlphaFold2 (ColabFold) or Protenix-mini. Each structure is searched against PDB and the AlphaFold/Swiss-Prot database with Foldseek, and each sequence is scanned with InterProScan and PSAURON. 3. **Score.** Four metrics, one per tool, are passed to 25 trained logistic regression models. The median predicted probability of being a curated gene model is the GeneStructor score. 4. **Rank.** Gene models are ranked within each gene by their score. The score difference between the top two models shows how clearly the best model stands out. ### Evidence used | Tool | Metric (column name) | What it captures | |---|---|---| | [AlphaFold2](https://github.com/sokrypton/ColabFold) | `plddt_80`: number of residues with pLDDT > 80 | Size of the confidently predicted, ordered region | | [Foldseek](https://github.com/steineggerlab/foldseek) | `bits.max`: maximum bitscore of the top hit against PDB or AlphaFold/Swiss-Prot | Structural conservation with known proteins | | [InterProScan](https://github.com/ebi-pf-team/interproscan) | `total_domain_length`: total length of InterPro or Pfam domains (whichever is larger), overlapping domains merged | Domain completeness | | [PSAURON](https://github.com/salzberg-lab/PSAURON) | `in_frame_score`: in-frame score (0–1) | Integrity of the coding sequence | ## Benchmark on rice ### AlphaFold2 or Protenix-mini | | AlphaFold2 (ColabFold) | Protenix-mini | |---|---|---| | Structure prediction | MSA-based; more accurate, slower | Protein language model, no MSA; much faster, slightly less accurate | | pLDDT metric | residues with pLDDT > 80 | residues with pLDDT > 70, used in place of pLDDT > 80 | | Used in rice for | training and evaluation on core rice genes | All rice gene loci in merged annotations | | `rank_isoforms.R` option | `--source alphafold` | `--source protenix` | The same 25 models are used for both. On the core rice genes, the two implementations ranked the same gene model first in 94.7 % of genes. ## Installation GeneStructor is a set of R scripts (with optional Python helpers); there is nothing to compile. **R (≥ 4.4)** with: ```r install.packages(c("data.table", "dplyr", "tidymodels", "glmnet", "bio3d")) # optional, for plotting gene models install.packages(c("ggplot2", "cowplot", "tidyr", "stringr")) ``` **External tools**, only needed to compute metrics for new proteins (versions used in the manuscript): | Tool | Version | Purpose | |---|---|---| | [ColabFold](https://github.com/sokrypton/ColabFold) (AlphaFold2) | 1.5.2 | Structure prediction | | [Protenix](https://github.com/bytedance/Protenix) (Protenix-mini) | 0.5.0 (esm) | Faster structure prediction | | [Foldseek](https://github.com/steineggerlab/foldseek) | 9-427df8a | Structure search | | [InterProScan](https://github.com/ebi-pf-team/interproscan) | 5 | Domain annotation | | [PSAURON](https://github.com/salzberg-lab/PSAURON) | 1.0.8 | In-frame score | The trained models can be obtained from [Zenodo](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23880730). ## Quick start: from .pdb files to ranked gene models The [`example/`](example/) folder holds the inputs for one rice gene, Os06g0113150, with two competing gene models: the RAP-DB model Os06t0113150-00 and the Gramene model OsNip_06G000900_01. It contains their AlphaFold2 structures (`structures/*.pdb`), the Foldseek, InterProScan and PSAURON results for the same proteins, and the gene models' coordinates (`Os06g0113150.gff3`) for plotting. ```bash git clone https://github.com/PGB-LIV/GeneStructor.git cd GeneStructor # 1. pLDDT counts from the structures Rscript scripts/structure_metrics.R --input-dir example/structures --out structure_metrics.csv # 2. combine all evidence into one table Rscript scripts/build_metrics_table.R \ --ids example/transcript_gene.tab \ --structure-map example/structure_map.tsv \ --structures structure_metrics.csv \ --foldseek-pdb example/foldseek_pdb.m8 \ --foldseek-afsp example/foldseek_afsp.m8 \ --interpro example/interproscan.tsv \ --psauron example/psauron_scores.csv \ --out metrics.tsv # 3. score and rank the gene models Rscript scripts/rank_isoforms.R --metrics metrics.tsv --source alphafold --out ranked.tsv # 4. plot the ranked gene models of the gene Rscript scripts/plot_ranked_gene.R \ --ranked ranked.tsv \ --gff example/Os06g0113150.gff3 \ --gene Os06g0113150 \ --out Os06g0113150.png ``` Step 4 needs the R packages `ggplot2`, `cowplot`, `tidyr` and `stringr`. It draws the CDS (and UTR, if present) features from the GFF3, colours each gene model by its source annotation and labels it with its rank and GeneStructor score. For your own genes, pass your merged GFF3 and any gene ID from the `Gene` column of `ranked.tsv`. The results should match [`example/expected_metrics.tsv`](example/expected_metrics.tsv) and [`example/expected_ranked.tsv`](example/expected_ranked.tsv). The Gramene gene model OsNip_06G000900_01 is ranked first (score 1.00), well ahead of the RAP-DB gene model Os06t0113150-00 (0.64). The longer protein it encodes folds with 1,374 confidently predicted residues and aligns almost completely to the structure of *Arabidopsis* callose synthase 10: ![GeneStructor ranking of the gene models at Os06g0113150](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df33a3e2-ed68-4c8f-a7d1-14d6aecf3378) ## Running on your own gene models ### 1. Transcript-to-gene table and protein sequences GeneStructor ranks gene models that share a parent gene, so it needs a tab-separated table linking each transcript to its gene (columns `ID` and `Parent`). With several annotations, merge them first so that overlapping gene models share a parent gene. For rice, RAP-DB genes were used as the reference, and Gramene and then RGAP gene models were assigned to a RAP-DB gene when they overlapped it on the same strand; otherwise they formed new genes. The merged rice annotation is on [Zenodo](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23880730). [`scripts/Simplified_GFF.rmd`](scripts/Simplified_GFF.rmd) extracts the table from a GFF3, and protein sequences can be extracted with, for example, [gffread](https://github.com/gpertea/gffread): ```bash gffread merged.gff3 -g genome.fa -y proteins.fa ``` Gene models that encode the same protein need only one structure. If you fold each distinct protein once, list which structure each transcript uses in a two-column table (`transcript_id`, `structure_id`) and pass it with `--structure-map`, as in the example. ### 2. Structures and pLDDT counts Predict one structure per protein with ColabFold or Protenix-mini, and name each file after the transcript (or structure) ID: ```bash colabfold_batch --msa-mode mmseqs2_uniref_env \ --num-models 3 \ --data \ --use-gpu-relax \ --amber \ proteins.fa structures/ Rscript scripts/structure_metrics.R --input-dir structures/ --out structure_metrics.csv --cores 8 ``` `structure_metrics.R` reads `.pdb` and `.cif` files. When building the metrics table, the ColabFold and Protenix file suffixes (`_unrelaxed_rank_001_…`, `_sample_0`) are removed and only the top-ranked ColabFold model is used. The Python parser [`scripts/process_colabfold_all.py`](scripts/process_colabfold_all.py) also reads ColabFold JSON files and reports pTM. ### 3. Foldseek ```bash foldseek databases PDB pdb tmp foldseek databases Alphafold/Swiss-Prot afsp tmp FMT="query,target,alntmscore,lddt,fident,alnlen,mismatch,gapopen,qstart,qend,tstart,tend,evalue,bits,taxid,taxname,taxlineage" foldseek easy-search structures/ pdb foldseek_pdb.m8 tmp --exhaustive-search -e 0.00001 --format-output "$FMT" foldseek easy-search structures/ afsp foldseek_afsp.m8 tmp --exhaustive-search -e 0.00001 --format-output "$FMT" ``` For each structure, the hit with the lowest E-value is used. If your species is itself in AlphaFold/Swiss-Prot, remove self-hits with `--exclude-taxon` in step 5 (for rice: `--exclude-taxon "Oryza sativa Japonica Group"`). ### 4. InterProScan and PSAURON ```bash interproscan.sh -i proteins.fa -f TSV -o interproscan.tsv -cpu 8 psauron -i proteins.fa -o psauron_scores.csv -p ``` ### 5. Metrics table and ranking ```bash Rscript scripts/build_metrics_table.R \ --ids transcript_gene.tab \ --structures structure_metrics.csv \ --foldseek-pdb foldseek_pdb.m8 --foldseek-afsp foldseek_afsp.m8 \ --interpro interproscan.tsv \ --psauron psauron_scores.csv \ --out metrics.tsv Rscript scripts/rank_isoforms.R --metrics metrics.tsv --source alphafold --out ranked.tsv # for Protenix-mini structures use --source protenix (pLDDT > 70 is used in place of pLDDT > 80) ``` ## Output `ranked.tsv` has one row per distinct gene model: | Column | Description | |---|---| | `Gene` | Parent gene | | `ML_rank` | Rank within the gene (1 = best); gene models whose scores round to the same value share a rank | | `transcript_id` | Representative gene model | | `transcript_id_collapsed` | All gene models of the gene with identical metrics (usually identical proteins) | | `median_pred_CT` | GeneStructor score: median probability of the curated class across the 25 models | | `prob_diff_to_rank_1` | Score difference to the rank 1 gene model of the gene | | `sd_pred_CT`, `n_models` | Spread of the 25 predictions and the number of models used | | `plddt_80` or `plddt_70`, `bits.max`, `total_domain_length`, `in_frame_score` | The metrics used | ## Interpreting the results - **Score difference.** A difference > 0.1 between rank 1 and rank 2 indicates considerable structural differences between the gene models and a strongly preferred model; these loci are the highest priority for curation. Smaller differences usually reflect small differences in protein structure. - **Very long gene models.** GeneStructor is not designed to distinguish one long gene from two falsely merged genes, especially when both parts fold into well-defined domains. - **Inspect the alignment.** For loci of interest, align the top-ranked and alternative structures to their Foldseek hits to see which parts of the known structure each gene model covers. ## Repository layout ``` GeneStructor/ ├── README.md ├── LICENSE ├── models/ logistic regression models ├── example/ quick-start inputs (rice gene Os06g0113150) and expected outputs ├── scripts/ │ ├── structure_metrics.R pLDDT counts from .pdb / .cif structures │ ├── build_metrics_table.R combine all evidence into one metrics table │ ├── rank_isoforms.R score and rank gene models with the ensemble │ ├── plot_ranked_gene.R plot the ranked gene models of one gene from ranked.tsv and a GFF3 │ ├── plot_single_gene_with_labels.R plotting functions (used by plot_ranked_gene.R) │ ├── predict_with_glm_ensemble.r ensemble prediction function (used by rank_isoforms.R) │ ├── process_interproscan_results.r total InterPro and Pfam domain length (used by build_metrics_table.R) │ ├── Simplified_GFF.rmd transcript-to-gene table from a merged GFF3 │ ├── process_colabfold_all.py pLDDT and pTM from ColabFold JSON/PDB and CIF files (Python) │ ├── process_cif_for_pLDDT.R pLDDT counts for the Protenix-mini run on all rice loci (HPC) │ ├── process_fs_protenix_all_nip.py top Foldseek hits for the Protenix-mini run (per-structure .m8 files) │ └── rename_chr_in_gff.r rename chromosomes (1 → chr01) in a GFF └── docs/ └── GeneStructor_Rank_isoforms.md walkthrough of the Protenix-mini ranking of all rice loci ``` ## Data availability The merged rice annotation, protein sequences, structure, Foldseek, InterProScan and PSAURON results, the training data and the trained models are on Zenodo: [10.5281/zenodo.23880730](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23880730). ## Citation and license If you use GeneStructor, please cite the manuscript above (the citation will be updated on publication) and the tools it builds on: AlphaFold2/ColabFold, Protenix, Foldseek, InterProScan and PSAURON. GeneStructor is released under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).

## 是什么

OneScience Examples 是一个由 OneScience 官方维护的 AI/ML 模型示例仓库，汇集了多种前沿模型的训练脚本、推理流程和运行环境配置，覆盖蛋白质结构预测、分子动力学、计算流体力学、天气预报等多个科学计算领域。它旨在为研究人员和开发者提供开箱即用的模型解决方案，每个子项目都包含完整的文档和代码。

## 亮点

- **覆盖面广**：仓库整合了生物科学、材料化学、天气预报、CFD、PDE 求解等多个领域的模型，便于跨领域对比和迁移。
- **标准化结构**：每个模型目录都包含 README、manifest.yaml、conf/、scripts/、train.py/inference.py，降低了上手和复现成本。
- **官方维护**：由 OneScience 团队维护，提供统一的下载脚本和运行流程，适合作为模型基准测试和二次开发的起点。
- **多模型支持**：在生物科学方向就包含 AlphaFold3、ESM、OpenFold、Protenix、RFdiffusion、ProteinMPNN 等主流模型，覆盖结构预测、序列设计、扩散生成等任务。

## 为何对本课题有用

该仓库直接服务于蛋白质结构 × AI/计算模拟课题，提供了多个核心模型的现成实现和运行示例：

- **结构预测**：AlphaFold3、ESM、OpenFold、Protenix、SimpleFold 等模型可用于蛋白质三维结构预测，是课题的基础工具。
- **构象生成与设计**：RFdiffusion（反向折叠扩散模型）、ProteinMPNN（序列设计）、TargetDiff、DiffDock（分子对接）等模型可用于构象采样、结构生成和序列设计。
- **分子动力学**：DeepMD、MACE、NequIP 等原子间势模型可用于 MD 模拟的加速和力场替代。
- **互作与功能预测**：MVGNN-PPIS（蛋白-蛋白互作）、GPSite（结合位点预测）等模型可支持蛋白-蛋白结合和功能预测。
- **可迁移思路**：即使不直接使用某个模型，其训练/推理流程、数据准备脚本和配置管理方式也可作为自定义 Pipeline 的参考模板。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：仓库根目录的 README.md 是总入口，每个模型子目录下的 README.md 提供具体使用说明。
- **安装与依赖**：通用依赖为 Python 3.10 + PyTorch，具体模型需参考各自 README 中的环境配置。依赖文件未在根目录统一列出，需进入各模型目录查看。
- **数据与权重**：大部分模型需要下载预训练权重和数据集，使用各模型目录下的 `download.sh` 脚本。
- **运行流程**：一般包括环境预检、数据准备、运行推理、验证输出。典型命令为 `cd models/<MODEL_NAME> && bash download.sh` 后按 README 执行。
- **输入输出格式**：不同模型输入输出不同，例如 AlphaFold3 输入为序列/多序列比对，输出为 PDB 结构；ProteinMPNN 输入为 PDB 结构，输出为设计序列。具体格式需参考各模型 README。
- **GPU 需求**：大多数模型需要 GPU 加速，尤其是 AlphaFold3、RFdiffusion 等大型模型，README 中会注明。
- **调试示例**：每个模型目录下通常有示例脚本和测试数据，可用于断点调试。

## 核心 idea

该仓库的核心价值在于“标准化封装”：将多个前沿科学计算模型统一为一致的目录结构、配置管理和运行流程，使得研究人员可以快速对比、复现和集成不同模型，而无需从零搭建环境。这种“模型即插即用”的设计理念，是它区别于单个模型仓库的关键。

## 可搬移点

- **模型实现**：可直接解耦并移植 AlphaFold3、RFdiffusion、ProteinMPNN 等模型的训练/推理代码到自定义 Pipeline 中，用于蛋白质结构预测、构象生成和序列设计。
- **数据准备脚本**：各模型目录下的 `download.sh` 和数据处理脚本可复用，用于获取和预处理 PDB、FASTA 等格式数据。
- **配置管理**：`manifest.yaml` 和 `conf/` 目录的配置方式可借鉴，用于管理模型超参数和文件清单。
- **运行流程模板**：标准化的 train.py/inference.py 结构可作为自定义模型开发的模板。
- **License**：仓库声明遵循各模型原始项目的许可证，具体需查看各模型目录下的 LICENSE 文件，是否允许自由移植需确认。

# OneScience Examples

欢迎来到 OneScience Examples 仓库！本仓库汇集了多种前沿人工智能/机器学习模型的示例代码、训练脚本和推理流程，涵盖蛋白质结构预测、分子动力学、计算流体力学、天气预报等多个领域。

## 项目简介

OneScience Examples 是 OneScience 官方维护的模型示例仓库，旨在为研究人员和开发者提供开箱即用的 AI/ML 模型解决方案。每个子项目都包含了完整的运行环境配置、数据准备脚本、训练/推理代码以及详细的使用文档。

## 可用模型

本仓库目前支持以下模型类别：

### 🧬 生物科学

| 模型 | 描述 |
|------|------|
| [AlphaFold3](./models/biosciences/AlphaFold3/README.md) | DeepMind 第三代蛋白质结构预测模型 |
| [AlphaGenome](./models/biosciences/alphagenome/README.md) | DNA 序列分析与变异评分模型 |
| [ESM](./models/biosciences/ESM/README.md) | ESMFold 蛋白质结构预测 |
| [Evo2](./models/biosciences/evo2/README.md) | 大规模基因组基础模型 |
| [OpenFold](./models/biosciences/OpenFold/README.md) | 开源蛋白质结构预测 |
| [PINNsformer](./models/biosciences/PINNsformer/README.md) | 物理-informed 神经网络 |
| [Protenix](./models/biosciences/protenix/README.md) | 蛋白质结构预测模型 |
| [ProteinMPNN](./models/biosciences/ProteinMPNN/README.md) | 蛋白质序列设计 |
| [RFdiffusion](./models/biosciences/RFdiffusion/README.md) | 蛋白质反向折叠扩散模型 |
| [scGPT](./models/biosciences/scGPT/README.md) | 单细胞转录组基础模型 |
| [SimpleFold](./models/biosciences/SimpleFold/README.md) | 轻量级蛋白质结构预测 |

### 🧪 材料化学

| 模型 | 描述 |
|------|------|
| [DeepMD](./models/matchem/DeepMD/README.md) | 深度势能分子动力学 |
| [eSEN](./models/matchem/eSEN/README.md) | 等变平滑能量原子间势 |
| [Equiformer V3](./models/matchem/Equiformer_v3/README.md) | SE(3) 等变图注意力原子间势 |
| [MACE](./models/matchem/MACE/README.md) | 原子间势能模型 |
| [MatRIS](./models/matchem/MatRIS/README.md) | 材料发现与结构预测 |
| [Mattergen](./models/matchem/Mattergen/README.md) | 材料结构生成模型 |
| [MatterSim](./models/matchem/MatterSim/README.md) | 通用材料模拟模型 |
| [NEP](./models/matchem/NEP/README.md) | 神经网络原子势能 |
| [NequIP](./models/matchem/NequIP/README.md) | E(3) 等变图神经网络原子间势 |
| [UMA](./models/matchem/UMA/README.md) | 统一分子架构 |

### 🌤️ 天气预报与气候

| 模型 | 描述 |
|------|------|
| [FourCastNet](./models/FourCastNet/README.md) | 图像天气预报模型 |
| [FuXi](./models/FuXi/README.md) | 气象预报模型 |
| [FengWu](./models/FengWu/README.md) | 气象预测模型 |
| [GraphCast](./models/GraphCast/README.md) | 图神经网络天气预报 |
| [Pangu-Weather](./models/Pangu_Weather/README.md) | 盘古气象大模型 |
| [XiHe](./models/XiHe/README.md) | 气象预测模型 |

### 💧 计算流体力学 (CFD)

| 模型 | 描述 |
|------|------|
| [CFDBench](./models/CFDBench/README.md) | CFD 基准数据集 |
| [DeepCFD](./models/DeepCFD/README.md) | 深度学习 CFD 模型 |
| [EagleMeshTransformer](./models/EagleMeshTransformer/README.md) | 网格图神经网络 |
| [GP_for_TO](./models/GP_for_TO/README.md) | 高斯过程优化 |

### 🎨 设计与生成

### 📐 偏微分方程神经网络 (PDENN)

| [DeepONet](./models/PDENNEval/DeepONet/README.md) | 深度算子网络 |

| [MPNN](./models/PDENNEval/MPNN/README.md) | 消息传递神经网络 |
| [PINN](./models/PDENNEval/PINN/README.md) | 物理-informed 神经网络 |

## 快速开始

### 1. 环境准备

每个模型项目都有其特定的环境要求。请参考各模型目录下的 README.md 获取详细的环境安装指南。

通用依赖：
```bash
# 基础环境 (根据具体模型可能需要额外配置)
conda create -n onescience python=3.10
conda activate onescience
pip install torch torchvision
```

### 2. 下载模型和数据

大部分模型需要下载预训练权重和数据集。使用各模型目录下的下载脚本：

```bash
cd models/<MODEL_NAME>
bash download.sh
```

### 3. 运行示例

参考各模型 README.md 中的运行流程，一般流程包括：

1. **环境预检** - 验证运行环境
2. **数据准备** - 下载和解压数据
3. **运行推理** - 执行预测
4. **验证输出** - 检查结果

## 项目结构

```
onescience-examples/
├── datasets/              # 数据集相关文档
├── models/              # 模型代码
│   ├── AlphaFold3/      # 蛋白质结构预测
│   ├── FourCastNet/    # 天气预报
│   ├── DeepMD/         # 分子动力学
│   ├── GraphCast/      # 图神经网络天气
│   ├── PDENNEval/      # 偏微分方程网络
│   └── ...             # 其他模型
└── README.md           # 本文件
```

## 文档说明

每个模型项目包含以下标准文档：

- **README.md** - 项目说明、安装指南、使用教程
- **manifest.yaml** - 模型文件清单
- **conf/** - 配置文件目录
- **scripts/** - 辅助脚本目录
- **train.py / inference.py** - 训练/推理入口

## 是什么
BioJava 是一个开源的 Java 生物信息学框架，用于处理生物数据，提供解析常见文件格式（如 FASTA、PDB、mmCIF）、序列与 3D 结构操作、分析统计例程以及常用算法实现。它旨在加速生物信息学应用的开发，尤其以 biojava-structure 模块对蛋白质结构的支持最为完善。

## 亮点
- **模块化设计**：按功能拆分为多个 Maven 模块（如 core、structure、alignment、aa-prop、protein-disorder 等），便于按需引入。
- **全面的格式支持**：支持 FASTA、PDB、mmCIF、UniProt、GenBank 等常见生物数据格式，并提供解析与写入。
- **3D 结构操作**：biojava-structure 模块提供蛋白质结构的表示、比对、二级结构分配、结构比对等丰富功能。
- **算法实现**：包含序列比对（Needleman-Wunsch、Smith-Waterman）、系统发育树构建、蛋白质性质计算等。
- **活跃社区与文档**：提供教程、Cookbook 和 API 文档，便于上手。

## 为何对本课题有用
BioJava 是蛋白质结构 × AI/计算模拟课题的**基础工具库**，其价值在于：
- **结构数据处理**：为蛋白质结构预测、构象采样、分子对接等任务提供 PDB/mmCIF 解析、结构操作和特征提取的 Java 实现，可作为数据预处理或后处理环节。
- **序列与结构比对**：提供序列比对和结构比对算法，可用于评估预测结构质量（如 RMSD、TM-score 计算）或构建训练数据集。
- **蛋白质性质计算**：aa-prop 模块可计算氨基酸组成、电荷、疏水性等，为特征工程提供支持。
- **可迁移思路**：其模块化设计、格式解析器（如 PDB 解析器）和结构对象模型，可被借鉴或直接用于构建自定义的蛋白质结构分析 Pipeline。

## 怎么用
- **主入口**：无单一主程序，作为库使用。可通过 Maven 引入依赖，例如在 pom.xml 中添加 `org.biojava:biojava-core` 和 `org.biojava:biojava-structure`。
- **安装与依赖**：使用 Maven 构建，依赖见各模块 pom.xml（如 biojava-structure 依赖 ciftools、mmtf 等）。需要 JDK 11+。
- **输入输出格式**：支持 FASTA、PDB、mmCIF、UniProt 等。例如，`StructureIO` 类可读取 PDB 文件，`ProteinSequence` 类处理序列。
- **GPU 需求**：无需 GPU，纯 CPU 计算。
- **Demo/示例**：各模块有 demo 包，如 `biojava-aa-prop/src/main/java/demo/BioJavaAADemo.java`、`biojava-alignment/src/main/java/demo/DemoAlignProteins.java`，可直接运行调试。测试类位于各模块 `src/test` 下。

## 核心 idea
BioJava 的核心在于**提供统一、可扩展的生物数据对象模型**（如 `Structure`、`Chain`、`Group`、`Atom`），将复杂的生物数据（序列、结构、注释）抽象为 Java 对象，并围绕这些对象提供丰富的操作算法，从而让开发者无需关注底层格式细节，快速构建生物信息学应用。

## 可搬移点
- **PDB/mmCIF 解析器**：`biojava-structure` 中的 `StructureIO` 和 `PDBFileParser` 等类，可解耦出来用于读取蛋白质结构文件，为 AI 模型提供输入数据。
- **结构比对算法**：`biojava-structure` 中的结构比对（如 `StructureAlignment`）可移植用于评估预测结构。
- **序列比对实现**：`biojava-alignment` 中的 Needleman-Wunsch 和 Smith-Waterman 实现，可移植用于序列特征提取或序列设计。
- **蛋白质性质计算**：`biojava-aa-prop` 中的 `AminoAcidProperties` 类，可计算氨基酸组成、电荷等，用于特征工程。
- **License**：LGPL 2.1，允许在开源或闭源项目中引用，但修改后的库需以 LGPL 发布（需确认具体条款）。

# Welcome to ![Build](https://github.com/biojava/biojava/actions/workflows/master.yml/badge.svg) [![Version](http://img.shields.io/badge/version-7.3.0-blue.svg?style=flat)](https://github.com/biojava/biojava/releases/tag/biojava-7.3.0) [![License](http://img.shields.io/badge/license-LGPL_2.1-blue.svg?style=flat)](https://github.com/biojava/biojava/blob/master/LICENSE) [![Join the chat at https://gitter.im/biojava/biojava](https://badges.gitter.im/biojava/biojava.svg)](https://gitter.im/biojava/biojava?utm_source=badge&utm_medium=badge&utm_campaign=pr-badge&utm_content=badge) BioJava is an open-source project dedicated to providing a Java framework for **processing biological data**. It provides analytical and statistical routines, parsers for common file formats, reference implementations of popular algorithms, and allows the manipulation of sequences and 3D structures. The goal of the biojava project is to facilitate rapid application development for bioinformatics. Please visit our [homepage](http://biojava.org/). ### Documentation The [BioJava tutorial](https://github.com/biojava/biojava-tutorial) is a great place to get started. It is most complete for the biojava-structure module. The [BioJava Cookbook](http://biojava.org/wiki/BioJava:CookBook4.0/) contains an older and slightly outdated collection of simple examples that teach the basics for how to work with BioJava. Full javadocs are available at the [BioJava website](http://biojava.org/docs/api). ### Maven Repository BioJava release are available from Maven Central. ### Quick Installation If you are using Maven you can add the BioJava repository by adding the following XML to your project pom.xml file: ```xml org.biojava biojava-core 7.3.0 ``` ### For developers Release biojava to maven central: - `mvn -Prelease release:prepare` - `mvn -Prelease release:perform` Publish new javadocs: - `mvn -Prelease site` this will write `target/site` - Push the contents of `target/site/apidocs` to the [biojava.github.io repo](https://github.com/biojava/biojava.github.io) under directory `docs/apiM.m.p` (e.g. docs/api7.1.4) and then link `docs/api` to `docs/apiM.m.p`, for it to be published in biojava.org ### Mailing Lists BioJava has one main mailing list. In order to avoid SPAM the list only accepts postings from list members. Anybody can become a list member, so please subscribe before you post. If you send without being subscribed your mail might get stuck in the moderation loop, which can cause several weeks of delay (no fun to read through all that spam). #### biojava-l general discussion list * [biojava-l@biojava.org](http://lists.open-bio.org/mailman/listinfo/biojava-l) This list is intended for general discussion, advice, questions, offers of help, announcements, expressions of appreciation, bugs found in release code and requests for features. #### biojava-dev developers list A [dev mailing list](http://lists.open-bio.org/mailman/listinfo/biojava-dev) used to exist, but it has now been shut down. For dev discussions we now use github issues. Please search existing issues and if you don't find the answer to your question submit a new issue. ### Please cite **BioJava 5: A community driven open-source bioinformatics library**
*Aleix Lafita, Spencer Bliven, Andreas Prlić, Dmytro Guzenko, Peter W. Rose, Anthony Bradley, Paolo Pavan, Douglas Myers-Turnbull, Yana Valasatava, Michael Heuer, Matt Larson, Stephen K. Burley, Jose M. Duarte*
[PLOS Computational Biology 15(2): e1006791](http://dx.plos.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1006791)

one_liner: HOOMD-blue 是一个通用的粒子系统分子动力学和蒙特卡洛模拟引擎，虽非蛋白质专用，但其MD模拟方法可迁移用于蛋白质结构计算研究。
readme:
[![HOOMD-blue](sphinx-doc/hoomdblue-logo-horizontal.svg)](https://glotzerlab.engin.umich.edu/hoomd-blue/)

[![Citing HOOMD](https://img.shields.io/badge/cite-hoomd-blue.svg)](https://hoomd-blue.readthedocs.io/en/latest/citing.html)
[![conda-forge](https://img.shields.io/conda/vn/conda-forge/hoomd.svg?style=flat)](https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/hoomd)
[![conda-forge Downloads](https://img.shields.io/conda/dn/conda-forge/hoomd.svg?style=flat)](https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/hoomd)
[![Read the Docs](https://img.shields.io/readthedocs/hoomd-blue/latest.svg)](https://hoomd-blue.readthedocs.io/en/latest/?badge=latest)
[![Contributors](https://img.shields.io/github/contributors-anon/glotzerlab/hoomd-blue.svg?style=flat)](https://hoomd-blue.readthedocs.io/en/latest/credits.html)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-BSD--3--Clause-green.svg)](LICENSE)

**HOOMD-blue** is a Python package that runs simulations of particle systems on CPUs and GPUs. It
performs hard particle Monte Carlo simulations of a variety of shape classes and molecular dynamics
simulations of particles with a range of pair, bond, angle, and other potentials. Many features are
targeted at the soft matter research community, though the code is general and capable of many
types of particle simulations.

## Resources

- [Documentation](https://hoomd-blue.readthedocs.io/):
  Tutorial, full Python API description, and usage information.
- [Citing HOOMD-blue](https://hoomd-blue.readthedocs.io/en/latest/citing.html)
  How to cite the code.
- [Installation guide](INSTALLING.rst):
  Instructions for installing **HOOMD-blue** binaries.
- [Compilation guide](BUILDING.rst):
  Instructions for compiling **HOOMD-blue**.
- [HOOMD-blue discussion board](https://github.com/glotzerlab/hoomd-blue/discussions/):
  Ask the **HOOMD-blue** user community for help.
- [HOOMD-blue website](https://glotzerlab.engin.umich.edu/hoomd-blue/):
  Additional information and publications.
- [HOOMD-blue benchmark scripts](https://github.com/glotzerlab/hoomd-benchmarks):
  Scripts to evaluate the performance of HOOMD-blue simulations.
- [HOOMD-blue validation tests](https://github.com/glotzerlab/hoomd-validation):
  Scripts to validate that HOOMD-blue performs accurate simulations.

## Related tools

- [hoomd-rs](https://hoomd-rs.readthedocs.io/):
  Infinitely customizable MC/MD simulations and order parameter computations in Rust.
  **Faster** than HOOMD-blue in most benchmarks.
- [freud](https://freud.readthedocs.io/):
  Analyze HOOMD-blue simulation results with the **freud** Python library.
- [signac](https://signac.readthedocs.io/):
  Manage your workflow with **signac**.
- [Molecular Simulation Design Framework (MoSDeF)] tools:

  - [`mbuild`]: Assemble reusable components into complex molecular systems.
  - [`foyer`]: Perform atom-typing and define classical molecular modeling force fields.
  - [`gmso`]: A flexible and mutable data structure for chemical topologies that writes HOOMD-blue formats.

[Molecular Simulation Design Framework (MoSDeF)]: https://mosdef.org/
[`mbuild`]: https://mbuild.mosdef.org/
[`foyer`]: https://foyer.mosdef.org/
[`gmso`]: https://gmso.mosdef.org/

## Example scripts

These examples demonstrate some of the Python API.

Hard particle Monte Carlo:
```python
import hoomd

mc = hoomd.hpmc.integrate.ConvexPolyhedron()
mc.shape['octahedron'] = dict(vertices=[
    (-0.5, 0, 0),
    (0.5, 0, 0),
    (0, -0.5, 0),
    (0, 0.5, 0),
    (0, 0, -0.5),
    (0, 0, 0.5),
])

cpu = hoomd.device.CPU()
sim = hoomd.Simulation(device=cpu, seed=20)
sim.operations.integrator = mc
# The tutorial describes how to construct an initial configuration 'init.gsd'.
sim.create_state_from_gsd(filename='init.gsd')

sim.run(1e5)
```

Molecular dynamics:
```python
import hoomd

cell = hoomd.md.nlist.Cell(buffer=0.4)
lj = hoomd.md.pair.LJ(nlist=cell)
lj.params[('A', 'A')] = dict(epsilon=1, sigma=1)
lj.r_cut[('A', 'A')] = 2.5

integrator = hoomd.md.Integrator(dt=0.005)
integrator.forces.append(lj)
bussi = hoomd.md.methods.thermostats.Bussi(kT=1.5)
nvt = hoomd.md.methods.ConstantVolume(filter=hoomd.filter.All(), thermostat=bussi)
integrator.methods.append(nvt)

gpu = hoomd.device.GPU()
sim = hoomd.Simulation(device=gpu)
sim.operations.integrator = integrator
# The tutorial describes how to construct an initial configuration 'init.gsd'.
sim.create_state_from_gsd(filename='init.gsd')
sim.state.thermalize_particle_momenta(filter=hoomd.filter.All(), kT=1.5)

sim.run(1e5)
```

one_liner: Moltemplate 是一个用于构建 LAMMPS 分子模拟体系的通用分子构建工具，支持粗粒化和全原子模型，虽非蛋白质专用，但可迁移用于蛋白质 MD 模拟的体系搭建。
card:
## 是什么

Moltemplate 是一个跨平台的、基于文本的通用分子构建工具，专门用于为 LAMMPS 分子动力学模拟生成输入文件。它最初设计用于构建自定义的粗粒化分子模型，但同样支持全原子模拟，并兼容多种力场（如 OPLSAA、AMBER、DREIDING、TraPPE 等）和分子模型（如 MOLC、mW、ELBA、oxDNA2）。

## 亮点

- **通用性与灵活性**：支持从粗粒化到全原子的多种模型，用户可通过文本文件（LT 格式）定义分子拓扑和力场参数，无需编写代码。
- **丰富的力场支持**：内置多种主流力场，并可通过第三方工具（如 ATB、Open Babel、AmberTools）生成输入，降低建模门槛。
- **跨平台**：基于 Python 和 Bash，可在 Linux、macOS、Windows 上运行，易于集成到现有工作流。
- **模块化设计**：提供多个独立脚本（如 moltemplate.sh、ltemplify.py、genpoly_lt.py），支持从 PDB/XYZ 文件转换、聚合物生成等任务。
- **活跃的社区与文档**：包含约 50 个示例和详细手册，便于学习和调试。

## 为何对本课题有用

Moltemplate 直接服务于蛋白质结构 × AI/计算模拟课题中的分子动力学（MD）模拟环节。它能够将蛋白质的原子坐标（如 PDB 文件）转换为 LAMMPS 可执行的输入文件，并自动分配力场参数，这对于进行蛋白质构象采样、蛋白-配体相互作用或蛋白-蛋白结合的 MD 模拟至关重要。此外，其粗粒化建模能力可用于构建蛋白质的简化模型，加速大规模构象搜索。对于 AI 生成的结构，Moltemplate 可作为后处理工具，将预测的坐标转换为可模拟的体系，从而验证或优化 AI 模型输出。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：`moltemplate.sh` 脚本，典型用法：`moltemplate.sh [-atomstyle style] [-pdb/-xyz coord_file] [-vmd] system.lt`。
- **安装**：通过 pip 安装（`pip3 install .`）或 conda（`conda install conda-forge::moltemplate`）。依赖 Python 3.4+、NumPy 和 Bash。
- **输入格式**：LT 格式（文本文件，定义分子拓扑和力场），支持从 PDB/XYZ 文件转换（使用 `ltemplify.py` 或 `mol22lt.py`）。
- **输出**：LAMMPS DATA 文件（.lmpdat），可直接用于 LAMMPS 模拟。
- **示例**：仓库包含约 50 个示例，位于 `examples/` 目录，每个示例有 README 和运行脚本，适合断点调试。
- **GPU 需求**：Moltemplate 本身不需要 GPU，但生成的 LAMMPS 模拟可能需要 GPU 加速（取决于 LAMMPS 配置）。

## 核心 idea

Moltemplate 的核心方法学在于将分子拓扑和力场参数抽象为可复用的文本模板（LT 格式），通过脚本自动展开为 LAMMPS 输入，从而将建模过程从繁琐的手工编码中解放出来，实现高效、可重复的分子体系构建。

## 可搬移点

- **LT 格式解析器**：`moltemplate/ltemplate.py` 等模块负责解析 LT 文件，可被解耦用于自定义的分子拓扑生成流程。
- **力场参数库**：`moltemplate/force_fields/` 目录下的力场文件（如 OPLSAA、AMBER）可直接复用，用于其他模拟软件或自定义 Pipeline。
- **文件转换工具**：`ltemplify.py` 和 `mol22lt.py` 可将 PDB/MOL2 文件转换为 LT 格式，可移植到其他需要分子坐标转换的场景。
- **License**：MIT 许可，允许自由使用和修改，但需确认具体文件（如 `ttree_lex.py` 使用 PSF 许可）的兼容性。

Moltemplate
===========

##  Description

[Moltemplate](https://moltemplate.org)
is a *general* cross-platform text-based molecule builder for
[**LAMMPS**](https://lammps.sandia.gov).
Moltemplate was intended for building custom coarse-grained molecular models,
but it can be used to prepare realistic all-atom simulations as well.
It currently supports the
[**ATB**](https://atb.uq.edu.au) molecule database, the
[**OPLSAA**(2023)](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/suppl/10.1021/acs.jpcb.3c06602),
[**OPLSUA**(2008)](./examples/all_atom/legacy_force_field_examples/force_field_OPLSUA_united_atom_2008),
[**LOPLS**(2015)](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpcb.5b08569),
[**AMBER**(GAFF,GAFF2)](./examples/all_atom/force_field_AMBER),
[**DREIDING**](./examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING),
[**COMPASS**](./examples/all_atom/force_field_COMPASS),
[**TraPPE**(1998)](./examples/coarse_grained/solvent_models/manybodywaterMW+hydrocarbonsTraPPE),
[**EFF**](./examples/misc_examples/explicit_electrons/eff_CH4),
force fields,
and the
[**MOLC**](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2019/cp/c9cp04120f),
[**mW**](https://doi.org/10.1021/jp805227c),
[**ELBA**(water)](./examples/coarse_grained/solvent_models/ELBAwater%2Bmethanol),
and
[**oxDNA2**](https://dna.physics.ox.ac.uk/index.php/DNA_model_introduction),
molecular models (and others).
(New force fields and examples are added continually by users.)
Moltemplate is inter-operable with
[**ATB**](https://atb.uq.edu.au),
[**Open Babel**](https://open-babel.readthedocs.io/en/latest/FileFormats/The_LAMMPS_data_format.html),
[**AmberTools**](https://ambermd.org/AmberTools.php),
[**LigParGen**](https://moltemplate.org/doc/moltemplate_talk_2019-8-15.pdf#page=191),
[**RED-server**](https://upjv.q4md-forcefieldtools.org),
[**VMD**](https://www.ks.uiuc.edu/Research/vmd),
[**topotools**](https://sites.google.com/site/akohlmey/software/topotools/tutorial-introduction),
[**PACKMOL**](http://m3g.iqm.unicamp.br/packmol/home.shtml),
[**EMC**](http://montecarlo.sourceforge.net/),
[**CellPACK**](http://www.cellpack.org),
[**Vipster**](https://sgsaenger.github.io/vipster),
[**struc2lammpsdf**](https://nanohub.org/resources/struc2lammpsdf),
and any other program that generates [**MOL2**](https://github.com/UnixJunkie/mol2-file-format-spec/blob/master/mol2.pdf) or [**LAMMPS DATA**](https://docs.lammps.org/2001/data_format.html) (.lmpdat) files *(by using the [mol22lt.py](https://github.com/jewettaij/moltemplate/blob/master/doc/doc_mol22lt.md) and [ltemplify.py](https://github.com/jewettaij/moltemplate/blob/master/doc/doc_ltemplify.md) file converters)*.


This repository contains 3 folders:
- [moltemplate](./moltemplate/): source code and force fields
- [doc](./doc/): documentation for moltemplate.sh, ltemplify.py, genpoly_lt.py, etc..
- [examples](./examples/): examples built with moltemplate


### Documentation

The best way to learn how to use moltemplate is to find an example
which is similar to the system that you wish to simulate and modify it.
This repository includes approximately 50 [examples](./examples).
Some of the moltemplate examples are also demonstrated (with pictures)
[here](https://moltemplate.org/examples.html).

All moltemplate users should read chapter 4 of the
[reference manual](https://moltemplate.org/doc/moltemplate_manual.pdf#section.4)
*(It's only 6 pages long. The first 3 chapters can be skipped.)*
Chapters 6, 7, and 5.1-5.3 also also recommended.
*(13 pages.)*

In addition, there are also several
[talks/tutorials](https://moltemplate.org/doc/talks.html)
online.


### Strategies for preparing all-atom simulations

Moltemplate was originally designed for preparing coarse-grained simulations.
Fully atomistic simulations usually require choosing
force-field specific atom types ("atom typing"),
and the calculation of atomic charge.
Moltemplate
[does not do this](https://moltemplate.org/force_field_recommendations.html).
Moltemplate also does not repair incomplete PDB files.
To get around these limitations:

* Users can use use *3rd-party molecule-builder tools* such as:
the [ATB](https://atb.uq.edu.au) database (LT format),
[AmberTools](https://ambermd.org/AmberTools.php) (MOL2 format),
[LigParGen](https://moltemplate.org/doc/moltemplate_talk_2019-8-15.pdf#page=190) (DATA format),
[OpenBabel](https://open-babel.readthedocs.io/en/latest/FileFormats/The_LAMMPS_data_format.html "Convert 3rd party sim files to LAMMPS DATA format"), and
[EMC](http://montecarlo.sourceforge.net/) (DATA format).
These tools can generate MOL2 or LAMMPS-DATA files
which can be converted into moltemplate format (LT format) using
[mol22lt.py](./doc/doc_mol22lt.md#mol22ltpy) or
[ltemplify.py](./doc/doc_ltemplify.md#ltemplifypy).
*(If you want to try and select the atom types
manually instead of using 3rd-party tools, read
[these suggestions](https://moltemplate.org/force_field_recommendations.html).)*
Alternatively, users can use the
[DREIDING force field](./examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING)
which has relatively simple
[atom type rules](./doc/DREIDING_Label_Manual.pdf).
* For atomic partial charges
the [RED-server](https://upjv.q4md-forcefieldtools.org)
is useful (which can generate a MOL2 file),
*in addition to the tools listed above*.
Alternatively, users can try using LAMMPS' built-in
[fix qeq](https://docs.lammps.org/fix_qeq.html) feature.



## Typical usage

```
    moltemplate.sh [-atomstyle style] [-pdb/-xyz coord_file] [-vmd] system.lt
```


## Installation Instructions

Moltemplate depends on other software to work
(such as BASH, python3, pip3, *or* conda).  Once these
dependencies have been met, installing moltemplate is relatively easy.
However many users find it difficult to install these prerequisites correctly.
A detailed installation guide is located [here](./INSTALL.md).


### Installation for conda users
If you have installed conda, you can download moltemplate using:
```
conda install conda-forge::moltemplate
```
This will omit the [moltemplate examples](./tree/master/examples)
and [documentation](./tree/master/doc).
You can browse examples [online](./tree/master/examples)
and/or download them using:
```
git clone https://github.com/jewettaij/moltemplate DESTINATION_DIRECTORY
```

### Installation for pip users

You can download moltemplate using:
```
git clone https://github.com/jewettaij/moltemplate DESTINATION_DIRECTORY
```
*(See below if you don't have git installed.)*
Then enter the directory where this README file is located:
```
cd DESTINATION_DIRECTORY
```
...and run the following command:
```
pip3 install .              # (or "pip", if that fails)
```
*(Note: In some environments, "pip3" is called "pip" instead.)*

If the command above fails (with both "pip" and "pip3"), then try this instead:
```
pip3 install . --user       # (or "pip", if that fails)
```
This will install moltemplate for a single user.
If you are on a shared computer and you want to install moltemplate
system-wide, then use:
```
sudo pip3 install .         # (or "pip", if that fails)
```
Later, you can uninstall moltemplate using:
```
pip3 uninstall moltemplate
# (use "pip" and/or prepend "sudo" if you did that earlier)
```
If this fails then read the
[installation troubleshooting guide](./INSTALL.md).
This guide will offer several different installation methods
and explain how to install the prerequisites needed.

***Note:***
*Alternatively, you can download and install moltemplate
using a single command:*
```
pip3 install git+https://github.com/jewettaij/moltemplate.git   # (or "pip", if that fails)
```
*...however this will omit all of the examples and documentation.*


## Web page

Additional suggestions and supporting code can be found at:

http://www.moltemplate.org


## Requirements

Moltemplate requires BASH and Python (3.4+), NumPy,
and can run on MacOS, linux, or windows.

*(Note: On MacOS, it may eventually become necessary to use 3rd-party tools
like "brew" to install BASH if apple removes BASH support in future updates.
Python 2.7 may also work, but you must edit your
[PATH](./INSTALL.md#Installation-method-2-Editing-bashrc)
to install moltemplate instead of using pip/pip3.
Pip no longer works with old versions of python.)*

To use LAMMPS and moltemplate, you will also need to install (and learn how to
use) a (unix-style) text editor.  (Word, Wordpad, and Notepad will not work.)
Popular graphical text editors
include **Atom**, **Sublime**, **Notepad++**, and **VSCode**.
Older, non-graphical programs include **vim**, **emacs**,
**nano**, **ne**, and **jove**.
(Apple's TextEdit can be used if you save the file as *plain text*.)

one_liner: MLatom 是一个面向原子级模拟的机器学习与量子化学开源平台，虽非蛋白质结构专用，但其 ML 势能、AIQM 方法和 MD 模拟等工具可迁移用于蛋白质结构计算。
card:
## 是什么

MLatom 是一个开源软件包，用于**原子级模拟**，结合了机器学习与量子化学方法（DFT、波函数和半经验近似）。它既可作为 Python 库使用，也可通过输入文件或命令行运行，支持本地执行或在线运行（无需安装）。其核心定位是提供一个统一的平台，让用户能够训练、使用和组合各种机器学习势能模型与量子化学方法，以进行能量、力、几何优化、分子动力学等模拟。

## 亮点

- **多方法集成**：集成了多种通用机器学习势（ANI、AIMNet2、MACE 等）和 AI 增强的量子化学方法（AIQM1、AIQM2、AIQM3、UAIQM），并支持通过接口调用 PySCF、Gaussian、ORCA、xtb 等外部量子化学程序。
- **丰富的模拟任务**：支持几何优化、过渡态搜索、IRC、频率与热化学计算、分子动力学（包括非绝热动力学）、光谱模拟（IR、Raman、UV-vis）以及周期性边界条件模拟。
- **灵活的模型训练**：提供统一的 `train()` 接口，支持对通用模型（如 ANI、AIQM1/2/3、UAIQM、OMNI-P1/P2x）进行微调，并支持主动学习、Δ-learning、迁移学习等高级训练策略。
- **跨语言实现**：核心部分包含 Fortran 和 Julia 实现（如 KREG 核岭回归），兼顾性能与灵活性。
- **易用性**：提供 Python API、输入文件格式和命令行工具，并支持在线平台（Aitomistic Hub、Aitomistic Lab@XMU），降低使用门槛。
- **持续更新**：活跃的开发社区，频繁发布新版本（如 3.27 引入 AIQM3），并支持通过 `pip` 安装。

## 为何对本课题有用

MLatom 直接面向**蛋白质结构 × AI/计算模拟**课题中的多个核心需求：

- **构象采样与分子动力学**：MLatom 内置的 MD 模拟（包括非绝热动力学）和 MDtrajNet-1（直接预测 MD 轨迹）可用于蛋白质构象采样和动态行为研究。
- **结构优化与过渡态搜索**：其几何优化和过渡态搜索功能可用于蛋白质局部结构精修或配体结合构象的搜索。
- **机器学习势能模型**：MLatom 支持训练和部署多种 ML 势（如 ANI、AIMNet2、MACE），这些模型可以用于蛋白质体系的能量和力计算，替代昂贵的量子化学计算，从而加速 MD 或构象采样。
- **AI 增强的量子化学方法**：AIQM1/2/3 等方法在保持半经验成本的同时达到接近耦合簇的精度，可用于蛋白质片段或配体-蛋白质复合物的高精度能量计算。
- **可迁移的模型训练框架**：其主动学习、Δ-learning 和迁移学习框架可以用于构建针对特定蛋白质体系的定制化 ML 势。

## 怎么用

- **安装**：`python3 -m pip install -U mlatom`，可选安装 PySCF、AIMNet2、ASE 等额外依赖。
- **快速开始**：
  ```python
  import mlatom as ml
  mol = ml.data.molecule.from_xyz_string('''3\n\nO    0.00000    0.00000    0.11779\nH    0.00000    0.75545   -0.47116\nH    0.00000   -0.75545   -0.47116\n''')
  aiqm2 = ml.methods(method='AIQM2')
  opt = ml.optimize_geometry(model=aiqm2, initial_molecule=mol).optimized_molecule
  print(opt.energy)
  ```
- **输入文件方式**：创建 `geomopt.inp` 文件，内容如 `AIQM2`、`geomopt`、`xyzfile=init.xyz`、`optxyz=opt.xyz`，然后运行 `mlatom geomopt.inp`。
- **在线运行**：无需安装，可直接在 Aitomistic Hub 或 Aitomistic Lab@XMU 上运行。
- **文档**：完整手册和教程见 [mlatom.com/docs](http://mlatom.com/docs)。
- **关键输入输出**：输入为分子结构（XYZ 格式），输出为能量、力、优化后的结构、轨迹等。

## 核心 idea

MLatom 的核心方法学在于**将机器学习模型与量子化学方法无缝集成到一个统一的模拟框架中**，通过 AI 增强的量子化学方法（如 AIQM1/2/3）在保持半经验成本的同时达到接近耦合簇的精度，并支持对通用模型进行微调以适应特定体系，从而在精度和效率之间取得平衡。

## 可搬移点

- **模型训练与微调模块**：`mlatom/models.py` 和 `mlatom/universal_mlips.py` 中的 `train()` 接口，可以解耦出来用于训练自定义 ML 势，并集成到自己的蛋白质模拟 Pipeline 中。
- **AIQM 方法实现**：`mlatom/aiqm1.py`、`mlatom/aiqm2.py`、`mlatom/aiqm3.py` 中的 AI 增强量子化学方法，可以作为高精度能量计算模块移植到蛋白质-配体结合能计算中。
- **分子动力学模块**：`mlatom/md.py` 和 `mlatom/namd.py` 中的 MD 和非绝热动力学实现，可以用于蛋白质构象采样。
- **几何优化与过渡态搜索**：`mlatom/simulations.py` 中的优化算法，可以用于蛋白质结构精修。
- **特征描述符**：`mlatom/EEEDDDD_descriptor.py` 和 `mlatom/EEEDDDD.py` 中的描述符生成代码，可以用于构建蛋白质结构的机器学习特征。
- **许可证**：Apache 2.0，允许自由使用、修改和分发，适合集成到学术或商业项目中。

**注意**：具体模块的接口和依赖需参考官方文档，README 未说明的部分需进一步查看源码。
readme: # MLatom MLatom is an open-source package for **atomistic simulations with machine learning and quantum chemical methods** — DFT, wavefunction-based, and semi-empirical approximations. Use it as a Python library, through input files, or from the command line — run it locally, or online with no installation. **[Website](http://mlatom.com)** · **[Documentation](http://mlatom.com/docs)** · **[Protomia](https://aitomistic.com/protomia)** · **[Aitomistic Hub](https://aitomistic.xyz)** · **[Aitomistic Lab@XMU](https://atom.xmu.edu.cn)** · **[Releases](http://mlatom.com/docs/releases.html)** ## Run online — no installation Run MLatom in your browser on either online platform — both powered by [Protomia](https://aitomistic.com/protomia), with an AI assistant for autonomous atomistic simulations: - **[Aitomistic Hub](https://aitomistic.xyz)** — free registration. - **[Aitomistic Lab@XMU](https://atom.xmu.edu.cn)** — free for academic users (registration with an academic email). ## Local installation MLatom is developed and tested on **Linux**, and that is the only platform it is verified on. It is often usable on macOS, but nothing there is tested: PyTorch, for one, publishes no build newer than 2.2.2 for Intel Macs, so you get an older PyTorch than the one MLatom is tested with. Windows is not supported. The [online platforms](http://mlatom.com/docs/cloud.html) above need no installation and are the way to run MLatom from any operating system. The easiest way to run MLatom is [online](http://mlatom.com/docs/cloud.html) — no installation. To install locally: ```bash python3 -m pip install -U mlatom ``` That pulls in the required dependencies automatically (including the PyTorch/TorchANI and geometry-optimization backends the **AIQM2** quick start uses). A few features need one more package — install only what you use: | for | install | | --- | --- | | PySCF methods: single point, TDDFT, frequencies and thermochemistry, densities, Raman | `pip install pyscf` | | AIMNet2 models | `pip install "aimnet==0.0.1"` (the version MLatom's interface targets; newer `aimnet` releases are a rewrite that does not work with the shipped models) | | format conversions (SMILES to xyz and back) | `conda install -c conda-forge openbabel` | | the ASE interface (ASE optimizers and dynamics) and MACE | `pip install ase` | | KREG_API backend (`ml_program='MLatomF'` needs none of this) | `conda install -c conda-forge mkl mkl-service` | | MDtrajNet | `pip install "e3nn==0.5.0"` (with e3nn 0.5.1 or newer, the published MDtrajNet-1 model produces different trajectories) | | MLTPA / DMC / hyperparameter search | `pip install rdkit` / `pyvibdmc` / `hyperopt` | AIQM2 additionally needs the DFT-D4 program, installed via conda: ```bash conda install -c conda-forge 'dftd4==3.6.0' # the version MLatom is tested against export dftd4bin=$(which dftd4) # point MLatom at the dftd4 executable ``` See the [installation guide](http://mlatom.com/docs/installation.html) for the full dependency list and other methods. ## Quick start Optimize the geometry of a water molecule with **AIQM2** — an AI-enhanced quantum-mechanical method (native to MLatom, CHNO elements) that reaches beyond-DFT accuracy at semi-empirical cost: ```python import mlatom as ml mol = ml.data.molecule.from_xyz_string('''3 O 0.00000 0.00000 0.11779 H 0.00000 0.75545 -0.47116 H 0.00000 -0.75545 -0.47116 ''') aiqm2 = ml.methods(method='AIQM2') opt = ml.optimize_geometry(model=aiqm2, initial_molecule=mol).optimized_molecule print(opt.energy) # optimized energy in hartree (≈ -76.3838) ``` The same calculation as an input file (`geomopt.inp`, with `init.xyz` holding the geometry): ``` AIQM2 # method geomopt # task: geometry optimization xyzfile=init.xyz # input geometry optxyz=opt.xyz # output geometry ``` ```bash mlatom geomopt.inp ``` Prefer zero setup? Run these online on the [Aitomistic Hub](https://aitomistic.xyz) or [Aitomistic Lab@XMU](https://atom.xmu.edu.cn) (both powered by [Protomia](https://aitomistic.com/protomia)) — no installation needed. ## Features & documentation Full manuals and tutorials are at **[mlatom.com/docs](http://mlatom.com/docs)** — begin with [installation](http://mlatom.com/docs/installation.html) and [get started](http://mlatom.com/docs/get_started.html). - **Methods** — universal ML potentials (ANI, AIMNet2); AI-enhanced QM methods ([UAIQM](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_uaiqm.html), [AIQM1](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_aiqm1.html), [AIQM2](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_aiqm2.html), [AIQM3](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_aiqm2.html)) approaching coupled-cluster accuracy at semi-empirical cost; and DFT, semi-empirical, and wavefunction methods via interfaces (PySCF, Gaussian, ORCA, xtb, MNDO, Turbomole, DFTB+, Sparrow, Columbus). - **ML models** — [train and use ML potentials](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_mlp.html) (KREG, GAP-SOAP, ANI, MACE, and more) with [active learning](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_al.html), Δ-learning, [transfer learning](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_tl.html), and self-correction. - **Simulations** — [geometry optimization](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_geomopt.html), [transition-state search](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_ts.html), [IRC](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_irc.html), [frequencies & thermochemistry](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_freq.html), [molecular dynamics](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_md.html), [nonadiabatic dynamics](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_namd.html), [IR](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_ir.html)/[Raman](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_raman.html)/[UV–vis](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_uvvis.html) spectra, and [periodic boundary conditions](http://mlatom.com/docs/tutorial_pbc.html). - **Workflows** — compose methods and tasks into complex pipelines from Python, input files, or the command line. ## How to cite If you use MLatom in scientific work, please cite: > Pavlo O. Dral et al. *MLatom 3: A Platform for Machine Learning-Enhanced Computational Chemistry Simulations and Workflows.* **J. Chem. Theory Comput.** 2024, *20*, 1193–1213. [DOI: 10.1021/acs.jctc.3c01203](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.3c01203) Feature-specific references appear in the program output and in [`CITATION.cff`](CITATION.cff). ## 是什么

Metagenomic-DeepFRI (mDeepFRI) 是一个用于蛋白质功能注释的高性能流水线，它结合了基于序列的 DeepFRI 深度学习模型和基于结构的 FoldComp 数据库（如 AlphaFold、ESMFold、PDB 等），通过 MMseqs2 快速搜索和接触图比对，为宏基因组基因目录提供快速、可扩展的 GO 术语和 EC 编号预测。

## 亮点

- **2-12 倍加速**：通过将 DeepFRI 模型转换为 ONNX 格式，并利用 ONNX Runtime 的优化，相比原始 TensorFlow 实现显著提升了推理速度。
- **结构-序列融合**：智能地利用预测结构（如果存在）进行 GCN 预测，否则回退到仅序列的 CNN 预测，兼顾准确性和鲁棒性。
- **分层数据库搜索**：支持多个 FoldComp 数据库（如 PDB、AlphaFold、ESMFold）的层次化搜索，优先使用实验结构，其次使用预测结构，提高覆盖率。
- **高度可配置**：提供丰富的命令行参数，支持自定义数据库、调整比对阈值、选择预测模式等。
- **跨平台支持**：通过 setup.py 自动下载并绑定 MMseqs2 和 FoldComp 二进制，支持 Linux、macOS 和 Windows（部分）。
- **内置基准测试**：提供 `benchmark` 子命令，可系统评估不同相似度区间对预测性能的影响。

## 为何对本课题有用

本仓库直接面向蛋白质结构 × AI/计算模拟课题中的**蛋白质功能预测**任务，是 DeepFRI 的工程化增强版。其核心价值在于：

- **结构信息的高效利用**：展示了如何将大规模预测结构数据库（如 AlphaFold DB）与深度学习模型结合，通过 MMseqs2 快速检索和接触图比对，为未知蛋白提供结构模板，从而提升功能预测的精度和覆盖度。
- **可迁移的加速方案**：将 TensorFlow 模型转换为 ONNX 并利用 ONNX Runtime 加速的思路，可迁移到其他蛋白质结构预测或构象生成模型（如 ESMFold、AlphaFold 的推理阶段），解决计算瓶颈。
- **模块化流水线设计**：其“序列搜索 → 比对 → 接触图生成 → 深度学习预测”的流水线架构，可作为蛋白质结构预测、分子对接或构象采样任务中特征提取和模板匹配的参考实现。
- **基准测试方法论**：提供的 `benchmark` 子命令和相似度分箱分析，可借鉴用于评估结构模板质量对预测性能的影响，适用于其他结构相关任务。

## 怎么用

- **安装**：`pip install mdeepfri`（默认 CPU 版），或 `pip install mdeepfri[gpu]` 以启用 GPU 加速（Linux x86_64）。依赖见 `pyproject.toml`，包括 `click`, `numpy`, `biotite`, `pysam`, `pyopal`, `foldcomp`, `onnxruntime` 等。
- **主入口**：命令行工具 `mDeepFRI`，由 `mDeepFRI/cli.py` 定义。
- **基本用法**：
  1. 下载模型：`mDeepFRI get-models --output path/to/weights -v 1.1`（v1.1 为微调版本，v1.0 为原始版本）。
  2. 准备结构数据库：首次运行会自动下载 PDB 数据库，也可手动下载其他 FoldComp 数据库（如 `afdb_swissprot_v4`）。
  3. 预测功能：`mDeepFRI predict-function -i /path/to/sequences.fasta -d /path/to/foldcomp/db -w /path/to/weights -o /output_dir`。
- **输入/输出**：
  - 输入：FASTA 格式的蛋白质序列文件。
  - 输出：`results.tsv`（主结果，包含蛋白、GO 术语、分数、网络类型等）、`prediction_matrix_*.tsv`（详细分数矩阵）、`database_search/`（各数据库搜索结果）。
- **GPU 加速**：默认自动尝试 CUDA，若不可用则回退 CPU。单实例 GPU 需约 2GB 显存。
- **测试**：`mDeepFRI/tests/` 包含单元测试，可通过 `python -m unittest mDeepFRI.tests` 运行。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学洞察：**通过将结构数据库检索与深度学习预测解耦，并利用 ONNX 优化推理，实现了“结构可用时用结构，不可用时用序列”的自适应功能预测，从而在保持精度的同时大幅提升吞吐量**。其创新点在于工程化地整合了 MMseqs2 的快速搜索、pyOpal 的全局比对、接触图生成和 DeepFRI 的 GCN/CNN 双分支模型，使得大规模宏基因组注释成为可能。

## 可搬移点

- **ONNX 模型转换与推理模块**（`weight_convert/convert_models2onnx.py` 和 `mDeepFRI/predict.pyx`）：可将 DeepFRI 的 TensorFlow 模型转换为 ONNX 并集成到自定义 Pipeline 中，加速其他蛋白质结构预测或功能预测模型。
- **接触图生成与比对模块**（`mDeepFRI/contact_map.py` 和 `contact_map_utils.pyx`）：可独立用于从 PDB 结构生成接触图，或用于结构比对任务。
- **数据库搜索与比对流水线**（`mDeepFRI/database.py` 和 `mDeepFRI/mmseqs.py`）：可复用其 MMseqs2 数据库构建和搜索逻辑，用于其他序列检索任务。
- **GO 术语传播与后处理**（`mDeepFRI/go_propagation.py`）：可借鉴其 GO 术语层级传播逻辑，用于其他功能注释任务。
- **License**：BSD 3-Clause，允许自由使用、修改和分发，但需保留版权声明。

[![GitHub issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/Tomasz-Lab/Metagenomic-DeepFRI.svg?style=flat-square&maxAge=600)](https://github.com/Tomasz-Lab/Metagenomic-DeepFRI//issues)
[![Docs](https://img.shields.io/readthedocs/metagenomic-deepfri/latest?style=flat-square&maxAge=600)](https://metagenomic-deepfri.readthedocs.io/)
[![Changelog](https://img.shields.io/badge/keep%20a-changelog-8A0707.svg?maxAge=2678400&style=flat-square)](https://github.com/Tomasz-Lab/Metagenomic-DeepFRI/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
[![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/pypi/dm/mdeepfri?style=flat-square&color=303f9f&maxAge=86400&label=downloads)](https://pepy.tech/project/mdeepfri)

*A pipeline for annotation of genes with [DeepFRI](https://github.com/flatironinstitute/DeepFRI),
a deep learning model for functional protein annotation with
[Gene Ontology (GO) terms](https://geneontology.org/docs/go-annotations/) and
mapping to [Cluster of Orthologous Groups (COG)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/research/cog) categories.
It incorporates [FoldComp](https://github.com/steineggerlab/foldcomp)
databases of predicted protein structures for fast annotation of
metagenomic gene catalogues.*

## 🔍 Overview

Metagenomic-DeepFRI is a high-performance pipeline for
annotating protein sequences with Gene Ontology (GO) terms using
[DeepFRI](https://github.com/flatironinstitute/DeepFRI),
a deep learning model for functional protein annotation.

Protein function prediction is increasingly important
as sequencing technologies generate vast numbers of novel sequences.
Metagenomic-DeepFRI combines:

- **Structure information** from FoldComp databases (AlphaFold, ESMFold, PDB, etc.)
- **Sequence-based predictions** using DeepFRI's neural networks
- **Fast searches** with MMseqs2 for database alignment
- **Significant speedup** of
[2-12×](https://github.com/Tomasz-Lab/Metagenomic-DeepFRI/blob/main/weight_convert/onnx_vs_tf2.png)
compared to standard DeepFRI implementation.

### 📋 Pipeline stages

1. Search proteins similar to query in PDB and supply `FoldComp` databases
with `MMseqs2`.
2. Find the best alignment among `MMseqs2` hits using `PyOpal`.
3. Align target protein contact map to query protein with unknown structure.
4. Run `DeepFRI` with the structure if found in the database, otherwise run
`DeepFRI` with sequence only.

![image.png](https://github.com/Tomasz-Lab/Metagenomic-DeepFRI/blob/main/docs/_images/mdeepfri-design.drawio.png)

### 🛠️ Built With

- [MMseqs2](https://github.com/soedinglab/MMseqs2)
- [pyOpal](https://github.com/althonos/pyOpal)
- [DeepFRI](https://github.com/flatironinstitute/DeepFRI)
- [FoldComp](https://github.com/steineggerlab/foldcomp)
- [ONNX](https://github.com/onnx/onnx)

## 📦 Requirements

- **Python:** >= 3.11, tested with 3.11 - 3.14 on Linux x86-64 and macOS (Apple Silicon)
- **Dependencies:** Automatically installed via pip

## 🔧 Installation

1\. Install from PyPI (Python 3.11 - 3.14). Wheels are available for Linux x86-64
and macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon. On Intel Macs pip builds from source, which needs
a C++ compiler with OpenMP (`brew install libomp`).

```{code-block} bash
pip install mdeepfri
```

The default install uses CPU ONNX Runtime and does not require CUDA.
On Linux x86_64, GPU acceleration may still be used automatically when a
compatible CUDA stack is already present on the system.

For an explicit, self-contained GPU install (Linux x86_64 only), use:

```{code-block} bash
pip install mdeepfri[gpu]
```

This pins ONNX Runtime 1.26 with CUDA 12 libraries bundled via pip
(`nvidia-cuda-runtime-cu12`, `nvidia-cudnn-cu12`, etc.). No system CUDA
toolkit upgrade is required, but an NVIDIA driver new enough for CUDA 12
is still needed.

2\. Run and view the help message.

```{code-block} bash
mDeepFRI --help
```

## 💡 Usage

### 1. Prepare structural database

#### 1.1 Existing `FoldComp` databases

The PDB database will be automatically downloaded and installed
during the first run of `mDeepFRI`.
The PDB suffers from formatting inconsistencies, therefore during PDB alignment
around 10% will fail and will be reported via `WARNING`.
We suggest coupling PDB search with predicted databases, as it massively
improves the structural coverage of the protein universe.
A good protein structure allows DeepFRI to annotate the function in more detail.
However, the sequence branch of the model has the largest weight,
thus even if the predicted structure is erroneous,
it will have a minor effect on the prediction.
The details can be found in
[the original manuscript, fig. 2A](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-23303-9/figures/2).

You can download additional databases
from [website](https://foldcomp.steineggerlab.workers.dev/).
During a first run, FASTA sequences will be extracted
from `FoldComp` database and `MMseqs2` database will be created and indexed.
You can use different databases, but be mindful
that computation time might increase exponentially with the size of the database.

Tested databases:

- `afdb_swissprot`
- `afdb_swissprot_v4`
- `afdb_rep_v4`
- `afdb_rep_dark_v4`
- `afdb_uniprot_v4`
- `esmatlas`
- `esmatlas_v2023_02`
- `highquality_clust30`

`ATTENTION:` Please, do not rename downloaded databases.
`FoldComp` has certain inconsistencies in the way FASTA sequences are extracted ([example](https://github.com/steineggerlab/foldcomp/issues/51)),
therefore pipeline was tweaked for each database.
If database you need does not work, please report in
[issues](https://github.com/Tomasz-Lab/Metagenomic-DeepFRI/issues).

`ATTENTION:` database creation is a very sensitive step which
relies on external software.
If pipeline is interrupted during this step, the databases might be corrupted.
If you are not sure about your database,
rerun the pipeline with `--overwrite` flag -
it will rerun database creation process.

#### 1.2. Custom `FoldComp` database

In order to use personal database of structures,
you will have to create a custom FoldComp database.
For that, download a `FoldComp` executable and run  the following command:

```{code-block} bash
foldcomp compress [-t number] <dir|tar(.gz)> [<dir|tar|db>]
```

### 2. Download models

Two versions of models available:

- `v1.0` - is the original version from DeepFRI publication.
- `v1.1` - is a version finetuned on AlphaFold models and machine-generated Gene Ontology Uniprot annotations ([details](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-63250-3)).

To download models run command:

```{code-block} bash
mDeepFRI get-models --output path/to/weights/folder -v {1.0 or 1.1}
```

### 3. Predict protein function & capture log

```{code-block} bash
mDeepFRI predict-function -i /path/to/protein/sequences \
-d /path/to/foldcomp/database/ \
-w /path/to/deepfri/weights/folder \
-o /output_path > log.txt
```

Other available parameters can be found upon command `mDeepFRI --help`.

## ✅ Results

The output folder will contain several files from different stages of the pipeline:

### Main Output Files

1. **`results.tsv`** - Primary output file containing
all functional predictions from the DeepFRI model.

2. **`alignment_summary.tsv`** - Summary of alignment statistics for
   each query protein, showing which queries were
   successfully aligned to database structures.

3. **`database_search/`** - Directory containing individual search results for
   each database queried:
   - `{database_name}_results.tsv` - One file per database searched
     (e.g., `pdb100_230517_results.tsv`, `afdb_swissprot_v4_results.tsv`)

4. **`prediction_matrix_*.tsv`** - Detailed prediction matrices for each
   ontology mode:
   - `prediction_matrix_bp.tsv` - Biological Process predictions
   - `prediction_matrix_cc.tsv` - Cellular Component predictions
   - `prediction_matrix_ec.tsv` - Enzyme Commission predictions
   - `prediction_matrix_mf.tsv` - Molecular Function predictions

   These files contain raw prediction scores for every protein × GO term
   combination and can be very large (>50MB).

5. **`query.mmseqsDB`** + associated index files - MMseqs2 database created
   from input query sequences.

### Primary Output Format (`results.tsv`)

The main output file contains the following columns:

- **protein** - Name of the protein from the input FASTA file.
- **network_type** - Type of neural network used for prediction:
  - `gcn` (Graph Convolutional Network) - Used when structural information
    is available from database alignment, providing more confident
    predictions.
  - `cnn` (Convolutional Neural Network) - Used when no proteins above
    similarity cutoff (50% identity by default) are found.
- **prediction_mode** - Ontology category: `mf` (Molecular Function),
  `bp` (Biological Process), `cc` (Cellular Component), or
  `ec` (Enzyme Commission).
- **go_term** - Predicted GO term identifier or EC number.
- **score** - DeepFRI confidence score for the prediction. Higher scores
  indicate greater confidence. See the
  [DeepFRI publication](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-23303-9)
  for details.
- **go_name** - Human-readable annotation from the Gene Ontology or EC
  nomenclature.
- **aligned** - Boolean indicating whether the query was successfully aligned
  to a database structure (`True`/`False`).
- **target_id** - Identifier of the matched database entry (e.g., `3al6_D` for
  PDB chain). Empty if no hit was found.
- **db_name** - Name of the database where the match was found
  (e.g., `pdb100_230517`, `afdb_swissprot_v4`).
- **query_identity** - Sequence identity percentage between query and hit
  (0.0-1.0 scale). Empty if no hit was found.
- **query_coverage** - Proportion of query sequence covered by the alignment
  (0.0-1.0 scale).
- **target_coverage** - Proportion of target sequence covered by the alignment
  (0.0-1.0 scale).

## ⚙️Features

### 1. Prediction modes

The GO ontology contains three subontologies, defined by their root nodes:

- Molecular Function (MF)
- Biological Process (BP)
- Cellular Component (CC)
- Additionally, Metagenomic-DeepFRI v1.0 can predict Enzyme Commission
  (EC) numbers.

By default, the tool makes predictions in all 4 categories. To select only a
few pass the parameter `-p` or `--processing-modes` few times, i.e.:

```{code-block} bash
mDeepFRI predict-function -i /path/to/protein/sequences \
  -d /path/to/foldcomp/database/ -w /path/to/deepfri/weights/folder \
  -o /output_path -p mf -p bp
```

### 2. Hierarchical database search

Different databases have different levels of evidence. For example, PDB
structures are real experimental structures and are considered highest quality
data. New proteins are first queried against PDB. Computational predictions
differ by quality (e.g., AlphaFold predictions are often more accurate than
ESMFold). You can search multiple databases hierarchically for flexibility.
For example, to search AlphaFold first, then ESMFold, pass the parameter `-d`
or `--databases` multiple times:

```{code-block} bash
mDeepFRI predict-function -i /path/to/protein/sequences \
  -d /path/to/alphafold/database/ -d /path/to/another/esmcomp/database/ \
  -w /path/to/deepfri/weights/folder -o /output_path
```

### 3. Temporary files

The first run of `mDeepFRI` with the database will create temporary files
needed for the pipeline. If you don't want to keep them for the next run, add
flag `--remove-intermediate`.

### 4. Skipping prediction matrices

By default, `mDeepFRI` writes detailed prediction matrix files
(`prediction_matrix_*.tsv`) containing raw scores for every protein × GO term
combination. These files can be very large (>50MB each). If you only need the
final `results.tsv` file and want to save disk space, use the `--skip-matrix`
flag:

```{code-block} bash
mDeepFRI predict-function -i /path/to/protein/sequences \
  -d /path/to/foldcomp/database/ -w /path/to/deepfri/weights/folder \
  -o /output_path --skip-matrix
```

### 5. CPU / GPU utilization

If argument `threads` is provided, the app will parallelize certain steps
(alignment, contact map alignment, functional annotation). GPU is often used
to speed up neural networks. By default, `mDeepFRI` runs on CPU. During
prediction it tries the CUDA execution provider first and falls back to CPU
if CUDA is unavailable.

**Technical tip:** Single instance of DeepFRI on GPU requires 2GB VRAM.

| Install | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| `pip install mdeepfri` | Default. Works without CUDA. |
| `pip install mdeepfri[gpu]` | Linux x86_64 with NVIDIA GPU; bundles CUDA 12 libs (ORT 1.26). |

**Troubleshooting GPU usage:**
If CUDA libraries are not found at runtime, you might see:

```bash
[W:onnxruntime:Default, onnxruntime_pybind_state.cc:1013 CreateExecutionProviderFactoryInstance]
Failed to create CUDAExecutionProvider. Require cuDNN 9.* and CUDA 12.*.
```

Try `pip install mdeepfri[gpu]` first. If the error persists, add library
paths to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`:

```bash
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:$(python -c 'import os, nvidia.cudnn, nvidia.cublas, nvidia.cuda_runtime; libs=[nvidia.cudnn, nvidia.cublas, nvidia.cuda_runtime]; print(":".join([os.path.join(m.__path__[0], "lib") for m in libs]))')
```

### 6. Structural template filtering

Templates whose global alignment to the query falls below
`--alignment-min-identity` or `--alignment-min-coverage` are discarded,
and the query falls back to the next database or the CNN.
Both filters are off by default.

### 7. Benchmarking

`mDeepFRI benchmark` measures how the similarity of the structural template
affects contact maps and predictions. Every database is searched once with
every query. For each `--identity-bin LOW HIGH` (MMseqs2 identity, `HIGH`
exclusive) one hit is kept per query and database - the best by bitscore,
or a random one with `--hit-selection random --seed 42` - and hits of a
query to itself are dropped unless `--keep-self-hits` is set. Contact maps
are built for every `--generate-contacts` value and, if weights are given,
GO terms are predicted. `--search-results` reuses the `database_search`
folder of a previous run.

```{code-block} bash
mDeepFRI benchmark -i /path/to/protein/sequences \
  -d /path/to/foldcomp/database/ -w /path/to/deepfri/weights/folder \
  -o /output_path -p mf -p bp -p cc \
  --identity-bin 0 0.5 --identity-bin 0 0.9 --identity-bin 0 1.01
```

The output contains `database_search/` with all MMseqs2 hits, `timing.tsv`
with the wall time of each stage and, per identity bin, the selected `hits/`,
their global `alignments/` with gapped sequences and one
`generate_contacts_<value>/` folder with the `predict-function` outputs.

## 🔖 Citations

Metagenomic-DeepFRI is a scientific software. If you use it
in an academic work, please cite the papers behind it:
- Bezshapkin, Valentyn, et al. "Scaling and democratising 
structure-based protein function prediction with metagenomic-deepFRI." bioRxiv (2026): 2026-04.
<https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.27.720983>

## 💭 Feedback

### ⚠️ Issue Tracker

Found a bug? Have an enhancement request? Head over to the
[GitHub issue tracker](https://github.com/Tomasz-Lab/Metagenomic-DeepFRI/issues)
if you need to report or ask something. If you are filing a bug, please

### 🏗️ Contributing

Contributions are more than welcome! See

for more details.

## 是什么

MolecularDocking 是一个由 Santiago Bolívar Ávila 博士维护的 GitHub 仓库，提供了一系列**开箱即用的 Google Colab 笔记本**和 Python 工作流，用于**分子对接**、**虚拟筛选**、**MM/GBSA 后对接重打分**以及**药效团分析**，主要面向计算化学和计算机辅助药物发现（CADD）领域。

## 亮点

- **一键启动的 Colab 笔记本**：所有工作流均以 Jupyter Notebook 形式提供，并配有 Google Colab 一键启动按钮，极大降低了环境配置门槛，便于快速复现和教学。
- **多引擎支持**：集成了 GNINA（GPU 加速）、SMINA 和 PandaDock 等多种对接引擎，用户可根据需求选择。
- **端到端流程覆盖**：从 SMILES 字符串的配体准备（`smile2dock.ipynb`）到对接执行、后对接分析、MM/GBSA 重打分、药效团映射，再到统计分析和可视化，形成完整的多阶段工作流。
- **后对接分析深度**：提供 GNINA 与 Vina 的对比评分、CNN score/亲和力分析、热图聚类、线性回归等分析工具，帮助用户深入理解对接结果。
- **模块化设计**：每个笔记本独立完成一个任务，可灵活组合成自定义流程，便于逐步替换和集成。

## 为何对本课题有用

该仓库直接面向**蛋白质-配体分子对接**这一核心课题，属于蛋白质结构 × AI/计算模拟方向的重要应用场景。其价值体现在：

- **直接可用的对接工作流**：提供了从配体准备到对接、重打分、药效团分析的完整工具链，可直接用于蛋白质-配体结合模式预测和虚拟筛选。
- **AI 与经典方法结合**：GNINA 本身是基于 CNN 的对接评分工具，仓库中的分析笔记本（`GNINA_and_Vina_Analysis.ipynb`）对比了 CNN 评分与经典 Vina 评分，展示了 AI 方法在对接中的应用。
- **后对接重打分**：Uni-GBSA 笔记本实现了 MM/GBSA 重打分，可提高对接结果的准确性，这对于构象采样后的能量评估至关重要。
- **可迁移的分析方法**：热图聚类、线性回归等统计分析方法可迁移到其他蛋白质结构预测或构象生成任务中，用于评估模型输出。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：所有工作流均为 Jupyter Notebook，可直接在 Google Colab 中打开运行，无需本地安装。
- **安装与依赖**：每个笔记本内部会安装所需依赖（如 `pip install`），具体依赖需查看各笔记本内容，README 未说明统一依赖文件。
- **输入/输出数据格式**：
  - 输入：蛋白质结构（PDB 格式）、配体（SMILES 字符串或 SDF/PDB 格式）、对接盒参数等。
  - 输出：对接 pose（PDB/PDBQT 格式）、对接分数（CSV 或表格）、热图（PNG）、药效团映射结果等。
- **GPU 需求**：GNINA 支持 GPU 加速，建议在 Colab 中启用 GPU 以获得更快速度；其他步骤 CPU 即可。
- **调试示例**：每个笔记本本身就是完整的示例，可直接运行并断点调试，例如 `GNINA_and_Vina_Analysis.ipynb` 提供了对比分析流程。

## 核心 idea

该仓库的核心方法学在于**将多种对接引擎和下游分析工具无缝集成到 Colab 环境中，形成一个模块化、可复现的虚拟筛选流水线**。其价值不在于发明新的算法，而在于**降低了计算药物发现的门槛**，通过标准化的工作流和可视化分析，使得研究人员可以快速从分子库筛选到候选化合物，并深入理解结合模式。

## 可搬移点

- **配体准备模块**（`smile2dock.ipynb`）：从 SMILES 生成 3D 构象并准备对接输入的逻辑，可解耦并集成到自定义的配体生成或筛选 Pipeline 中。
- **GNINA 对接执行模块**（`gninasminadocking.ipynb`）：调用 GNINA 进行 GPU 加速对接的代码，可作为对接步骤的参考实现，替换为其他对接引擎或集成到自动化流程。
- **MM/GBSA 重打分模块**（`UniGBSA_PostDocking_Colab_EN.ipynb`）：使用 Uni-GBSA 进行重打分的逻辑，可移植到需要更精确结合自由能评估的 Pipeline 中。
- **药效团分析模块**（`5_PharmacophoreToolkit_PostDocking_Colab_EN.ipynb`）：后对接药效团映射和相互作用分析，可用于筛选结果的过滤和解释。
- **统计分析模块**（`Heatmap_with_dendrogram.ipynb` 和 `Introduction_to_Docking_Data_Analysis_with_Linear_Regression.ipynb`）：热图聚类和线性回归分析代码，可迁移到任何需要分析对接分数或生物活性数据的场景。
- **License**：仓库采用 MIT 许可证，允许自由使用、修改和分发，但需保留版权声明。

## 是什么

openfe_analysis 是 OpenFreeEnergy 组织开发的一个 Python 包，专门用于分析 OpenFE 自由能计算（特别是 OpenMMTools `MultiStateReporter` 生成的 `.nc` 轨迹文件）的模拟结果。它通过提供一个 MDAnalysis Reader（`FEReader`），让用户能够以标准 MDAnalysis 接口加载多副本/多状态的轨迹数据，从而进行结构分析、RMSD 计算、约束分析等。

## 亮点

- **无缝集成 MDAnalysis**：通过自定义 `FEReader`，将 OpenFE 的 `.nc` 轨迹文件直接接入 MDAnalysis 生态，用户无需学习新 API 即可使用熟悉的 MDAnalysis 功能（如轨迹迭代、原子选择、写入其他格式）。
- **多副本/多状态处理**：明确支持从包含多个副本的 `.nc` 文件中按 Hamiltonian 状态或副本索引提取轨迹，解决了自由能计算中常见的多副本数据管理问题。
- **模块化设计**：代码结构清晰，分为 `reader.py`、`restraints.py`、`rmsd.py`、`transformations.py` 等模块，便于扩展和维护。
- **丰富的测试与文档**：包含单元测试（`tests/`）和 Jupyter 教程（`examples/`、`docs/tutorials/`），覆盖 Boresch 约束分析和结构分析等典型场景。

## 为何对本课题有用

本仓库直接服务于蛋白质结构 × AI/计算模拟课题中的**自由能计算**和**构象采样**分析环节。具体价值包括：

- **自由能计算轨迹分析**：OpenFE 是常用的相对结合自由能（RBFE）计算工具，本包提供了对 OpenFE 输出轨迹的标准化分析入口，可用于评估模拟收敛性、检查约束稳定性、计算 RMSD 等，是验证 AI 预测蛋白-配体结合亲和力的重要辅助工具。
- **构象采样分析**：通过 MDAnalysis 接口，用户可以方便地提取不同 λ 状态或副本的构象，进行聚类、PCA 等分析，有助于理解蛋白-配体结合过程中的构象变化。
- **可迁移的分析框架**：其 `FEReader` 的设计思路（将自定义轨迹格式适配到通用分析框架）可迁移到其他 AI 生成轨迹（如扩散模型生成的构象）的分析中。

## 怎么用

- **安装**：通过 conda 安装 `conda install -c conda-forge openfe-analysis`，依赖见 `environment.yml`（包括 MDAnalysis、netCDF4、openff-units、spyrmsd、rdkit 等）。
- **主入口**：核心类是 `openfe_analysis.FEReader`，用于加载轨迹。示例代码见 README：
  ```python
  import MDAnalysis as mda
  from openfe_analysis import FEReader
  u = mda.Universe("hybrid_system.pdb", "simulation.nc", format=FEReader, index=0, index_method="state")
  ```
- **输入/输出**：输入为 OpenFE 生成的 `.nc` 轨迹文件（由 OpenMMTools `MultiStateReporter` 创建）和对应的 PDB 结构文件；输出为 MDAnalysis Universe 对象，可进一步写入 XTC 等格式或进行各种分析。
- **测试与示例**：单元测试位于 `src/openfe_analysis/tests/`，包含 `test_reader.py`、`test_rmsd_classes.py` 等；Jupyter 教程位于 `examples/` 和 `docs/tutorials/`，如 `boresch_analysis.ipynb` 和 `structural_analysis.ipynb`，可直接用于断点调试。
- **GPU 需求**：本包本身不需要 GPU，但运行 OpenFE 模拟可能需要 GPU 加速（取决于 OpenMM 配置）。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学洞察：**通过自定义 MDAnalysis Reader 将多副本自由能轨迹数据透明地映射为标准的 Universe 对象，从而复用成熟的 MDAnalysis 分析生态**。其巧妙之处在于，`FEReader` 内部处理了 `.nc` 文件的多副本/多状态索引逻辑，使用户无需关心底层数据布局，即可像处理普通 MD 轨迹一样进行切片、迭代和分析，大幅降低了自由能计算轨迹分析的门槛。

## 可搬移点

- **`FEReader` 类（`src/openfe_analysis/reader.py`）**：最值得解耦的模块。其核心逻辑（解析 `.nc` 文件、处理多副本索引、实现 MDAnalysis Reader 接口）可被提取并适配到其他自定义轨迹格式（如 AI 生成的构象文件）的分析中。
- **`restraints.py` 和 `rmsd.py`**：提供了针对自由能计算中约束（如 Boresch 约束）和 RMSD 的专用分析函数，可直接复用或移植到自己的分析 Pipeline 中。
- **`transformations.py`**：包含轨迹变换逻辑，可用于数据预处理。
- **License**：项目采用 MIT 许可证（见 `pyproject.toml` 中的 classifiers），允许自由使用和修改，但需保留版权声明。

# openfe_analysis

[![Logo](https://img.shields.io/badge/OSMF-OpenFreeEnergy-%23002f4a)](https://openfree.energy/)
[![CI](https://github.com/OpenFreeEnergy/openfe_analysis/actions/workflows/ci.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/OpenFreeEnergy/openfe_analysis/actions/workflows/ci.yaml)
[![Coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/OpenFreeEnergy/openfe_analysis/graph/badge.svg?token=krb231ftki)](https://codecov.io/gh/OpenFreeEnergy/openfe_analysis)
[![documentation](https://readthedocs.org/projects/openfe_analysis/badge/?version=stable)](https://openfe_analysis.openfree.energy/en/stable/?badge=stable)
[![Powered by MDAnalysis](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-MDAnalysis-orange.svg?logoWidth=16&logo=data:image/x-icon;base64,)](https://www.mdanalysis.org)

## Quickstart

A package for the analysis of simulations performed using OpenFE (more specifically `.nc` files created by OpenMMTools `MultiStateReporter`).
This package provides a MDAnalysis Reader to start to explore your trajectory data:

```python
import MDAnalysis as mda
from openfe_analysis import FEReader

# A "simulation.nc" file contains multiple replicas, so we must choose which of these we load.
# Provide an index for the state or replica to extract.
# The `index_method` then determines whether `index` refers to a Hamiltonian ``state`` (following a single lambda state)
# or a ``replica`` (following a particular replica).
u = mda.Universe(
    "hybrid_system.pdb", "simulation.nc", format=FEReader, index=0, index_method="state"
)
```

For example to convert your trajectory to a different format for visualisation:

```python
import MDAnalysis as mda
from openfe_analysis import FEReader

with mda.Writer("out.xtc", n_atoms=len(u.atoms)) as w:
    for ts in u.trajectory:
        w.write(u.atoms)
```

## Installation

Installation is done via the conda package manager, simply:

```conda install -c conda-forge openfe-analysis```

For further guidance on using the conda package manager, please consult our [installation guide](https://docs.openfree.energy/en/stable/installation.html)

## 是什么

`cfoldseeker` 是一个基于蛋白质结构相似性搜索同源基因簇（gene clusters）的 Python 工具。它利用 `foldseek` 对查询蛋白结构进行结构同源搜索（支持本地和远程目标数据库），并通过获取每个蛋白编码序列的基因组位置（从远程交叉引用 API 或本地数据库）来识别这些同源命中中基因组共定位的基因簇。它是 `cblaster` 的结构相似性驱动姊妹工具，可原生生成 `cblaster` 风格输出和 `clinker` 可视化。

## 亮点

- **双模式搜索**：支持远程搜索（针对 AlphaFoldDB，利用 Foldseek webserver）和本地搜索（针对本地 foldseek 数据库），灵活适应不同场景。
- **本地聚类模式**：支持对预聚类序列集（MMseqs2）的代表性蛋白进行搜索，若代表蛋白命中，则考虑所有非代表成员，提高搜索效率。
- **紧密集成**：与 `cblaster` 和 `clinker` 深度集成，提供一致的输出格式和交互式可视化，便于下游分析。
- **辅助工具**：提供 `cfoldseeker-cds` 构建本地基因组上下文数据库，`cfoldseeker-seqs` 导出簇的 GenBank 文件，完善工作流。
- **社区资源**：提供 Zenodo 社区预生成输入文件，节省用户计算成本。

## 为何对本课题有用

`cfoldseeker` 直接服务于蛋白质结构 × AI/计算模拟课题中的**结构相似性搜索**和**基因簇挖掘**。它利用 `foldseek` 的快速结构比对，将结构预测结果（如 AlphaFold 模型）与已知蛋白结构数据库比对，识别同源蛋白，进而通过基因组共定位发现潜在的功能相关基因簇。这对于理解蛋白-蛋白互作、功能预测和进化分析具有直接价值。其模块化设计（远程/本地搜索、聚类模式）可被借鉴用于构建自定义的结构相似性搜索 Pipeline，或集成到蛋白结构生成/构象采样后的功能注释流程中。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：命令行工具 `cfoldseeker`（对应 `cfoldseeker/main.py`），辅助工具 `cfoldseeker-cds`（`build_cds_db.py`）和 `cfoldseeker-seqs`（`extract_sequences.py`）。
- **安装**：通过 PyPI 或 Bioconda 安装，依赖见 `pyproject.toml`（如 `biopython`, `cblaster`, `polars`, `networkx`, `requests`, `kegg-pull`, `gb-io`），需要 Python >=3.12。
- **输入/输出**：输入为查询蛋白结构（PDB 格式）和结构数据库（本地或远程）；输出为基因簇列表、cblaster 风格表格和 clinker 可视化。
- **GPU 需求**：README 未说明，但 `foldseek` 本身支持 CPU，远程模式无需本地 GPU。
- **调试示例**：README 未提供具体 Demo 或单元测试，但文档站点（readthedocs）可能包含教程；可参考 `cfoldseeker` 的模块结构进行断点调试。

## 核心 idea

`cfoldseeker` 的核心方法学洞察在于**将结构相似性搜索与基因组共定位分析结合**，通过 `foldseek` 的高效结构比对快速筛选同源蛋白，再利用基因组位置信息识别共定位基因簇，从而在结构层面发现功能相关的基因模块。其创新点在于将结构搜索的敏感性与基因组上下文的功能推断相结合，弥补了纯序列搜索的不足，为基因簇挖掘提供了结构驱动的全新视角。

## 可搬移点

- **`cfoldseeker/remote.py` 和 `remote_parsers.py`**：远程搜索和 API 解析逻辑，可解耦用于构建自定义的结构搜索客户端，支持 AlphaFoldDB 和 UniProt 等。
- **`cfoldseeker/local.py` 和 `local_clustered.py`**：本地搜索和聚类模式实现，可移植到需要高效结构数据库搜索的 Pipeline 中。
- **`cfoldseeker/classes.py`**：核心数据类（如基因簇、命中记录），可复用作为自定义分析的数据结构。
- **`cfoldseeker/build_cds_db.py`**：构建本地基因组上下文数据库的逻辑，可借鉴用于整合结构注释与基因组位置。
- **License**：MIT 许可，允许自由使用和修改，但需确认第三方依赖（如 `foldseek`, `cblaster`）的许可条款。
